  • Well, it’s time to stop mindlessly scrolling and start reading because team Cosmo tapped experts to break down the ideal skincare routine order that’s streamlined and effective for your exact concerns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Recent findings suggest that the world of skincare can promptly become confusing and overwhelming. Doom-scrolling through SkinTok makes things seem even more complicated. Like, how many steps do you actually need? Which serums are worth using? What products are totally superfluous? If you followed every bit of “foolproof” advice you found on the app, your skin barrier would be compromised and your complexion could look worse than before you went down this rabbit hole.

Well, it’s time to stop mindlessly scrolling and start reading because team Cosmo tapped experts to break down the ideal skincare routine order that’s streamlined and effective for your exact concerns.

In a recent development, trust us, it's a lot to consider even for beauty editors who spend their entire day testing all of these products, let alone a beginner just trying to get glowy, clear skin or deter fine lines. But step by step, we're gonna make sense of it all, below.

Recent findings suggest that first things first: You do not need a 10-step skincare routine (or even a 5-step routine!). "Less is more when it comes to your skin—I'm all about product reducing," indicates dermatologist Karan Lal, MD. "In reality, our skin chemistry needs hydration and moisture to maintain a good skin barrier, which you can get from just a few products." And, as virtually all dermatologists agree, those products include the following:.

That's it. The three most notable skincare products are cleanser, moisturizer, and SPF. It’s not glamorous, but good skin doesn’t need to be (just ask your dermatologist or anyone on the Cosmo beauty team—simple is always better). The more products you layer on, the higher your risk is for irritation, allergic reactions, and breakouts, notes Dr. Lal.

Industry observers note that now, if you're looking to build a slightly more advanced skincare routine, we're totally on board with that, too. Keep reading to learn how to incorporate more skincare steps, and what order they should be applied.

Sources indicate that “The rule of thumb when applying skincare is to apply the lightest formula first and the heaviest last since thinner products can’t penetrate thicker products,” indicates dermatologist Shereene Idriss, MD. Example: Layering a serum (thin) on top of your moisturizer (thick) would render that serum almost ineffective because it can't absorb into your skin when there's an occlusive barrier sitting on top of it.

Recent findings suggest that please, for the love of the beauty gods, remove your makeup and wash your face before slathering on your skincare products. “For ingredients to absorb properly, you need clean skin that’s totally free of oil and grime,” indicates dermatologist Mona Gohara, MD, which is where double-cleansing comes in.

Sources indicate that wondering how to double cleanse? The simplest method is to remove your makeup with a cleansing oil or balm (neither is "better" than the other; it's just personal preference). This step will dissolve all the makeup on your face without stripping your skin.

Then, follow that up with a gentle cleanser that works with your skin type. Dry skin should look for creamy, non-foaming face washes with barrier-boosting ingredients like ceramides, hyaluronic acid, and glycerin; while oily skin should try gel-based face washes or gentle foaming cleansers.

Those with acne-prone skin will benefit from a formula with added acne-fighting ingredients, like salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide. Keep in mind, though: If your skin is sensitive, use soothing formulas loaded with things like colloidal oatmeal, aloe vera, and niacinamide.

Recent findings suggest that it depends, but usually yes. If you have oily or acne-prone skin, then definitely yes—cleansing after you wake up is a good way to get rid of any grime or shine that's collected overnight. However, if you have dry or sensitive skin, you probs don't need to re-wash ahead of the rest of your routine, but if you're a sweaty sleeper, it's always a good idea to freshen your face before the rest of your skincare routine.

Face toners used to be terrible, alcohol-based liquids that burned your face. But today’s (good) toners are either filled with gentle, hydrating ingredients for dry and sensitive skin, or filled with chemical exfoliants to treat acne and bumps. “Toners are not meant to be something that sits around on your skin and feels heavy,” states Dr. Gohara. “They’re just priming your face for ingredients to be better absorbed later on.”.

According to recent reports, reminder: Toner (like most of the steps on this list) is optional, but if your toner smells like nail polish remover or alcohol, you need to ditch it—fast—and find an updated version instead. The best toner for acne-prone or oily skin is gonna be filled with ingredients that'll help unclog pores and prevent breakouts, like salicylic acid and/or AHAs. Tap it on your skin every other night (or morning, if you plan to use a retinol at night), then wait 60 seconds before layering another product.

If your skin is dry and/or sensitive, choose a toner with hydrating ingredients to reduce potential irritation (like hyaluronic acid, polyglutamic acid, squalane, ceramides, etc.). You can pat this onto your skin every morning, night, or both.

Toners and essences are pretty interchangeable in their consistencies, so if you’re looking for when to use your essence in your skincare routine, use it as step 2 (instead of toner). If you happen to have both in your routine, swipe on a toner first, then pat in an essence. (Think of it like a thin moisturizer-serum hybrid.).

Exfoliators keep skin smooth and clear by removing built-up dead skin cells and excess oil that can dull your complexion and block product absorption. They should be used after toner, when the skin is clean and balanced, and before serums so your treatments can penetrate more effectively.

There are two types of exfoliators: Chemical and physical. Chemical exfoliants use acids or enzymes (like AHAs, BHAs, or PHAs) to dissolve dead skin cells and are best for concerns like acne, clogged pores, uneven texture, and dark spots. Physical exfoliants use gentle scrubbing particles to manually buff skin smooth and can give instant results, but should be used carefully to avoid irritation.

Incorporate an exfoliator into your routine one to three times per week for ongoing skin concerns, especially if you have sensitive or acne-prone skin. Don’t forget to follow exfoliation with hydrating products and sunscreen during the day, too!

“Serums are essentially shots of extremely concentrated nutrients, hydrators, or antioxidants that really amp up your skin health as soon as you apply them,” claims Dr. Gohara. “People often skip out on using them, but they’re honestly the heavy lifters of your skincare routine.” So, while serums are totally optional, they’re often a good first step to leveling up your skincare routine and boosting your skin health.

Recent findings suggest that for almost all skin types, Dr. Gohara, Dr. Lal, Dr. Idriss, and every other derm in existence, swear by using a vitamin C serum in the morning, which protects your skin from inflammation and damage caused by environmental factors, while also brightening dark spots over time. Just note: Vitamin C can be strong, so if your skin is sensitive, use it every other morning (or every two mornings) instead.

Though serums are optional, all skin types can benefit from using a hydrating, hyaluronic-acid-based serum at night (and, honestly, in the morning too), which pulls water into your skin from the air to keep it hydrated. “If you’re using acne treatments or anti-aging products—which can be drying or irritating—you want to prep your skin with as much moisture as possible first,” claims Dr. Idriss.

Recent findings suggest that totally. But when it comes to layering serums, keep in mind the thin-to-thick rule, indicates dermatologist Jessie Cheung, MD. "Thicker serums may impede the absorption of the thinner formulations," she notes. So you'll want to start with your watery, vitamin C serums, then layer on rich, creamy formulas after.

Recent findings suggest that eye creams tend to be lighter and thinner than face moisturizers, so make sure to apply them before your creams and oils if you opt to use one. (Remember: lighter products go before heavier products).

According to recent reports, for morning use, look for an eye cream that's packed with caffeine, which helps temporarily constrict and tighten puffy under-eyes within 20 minutes. And, ideally, opt for one with a cooling applicator; “the cold steel helps with fluid retention—aka under-eye bags—especially if you keep the cream in the fridge between uses,” says Dr. Gohara.

“Most people think a night eye cream should contain retinol to help with fine lines, but in reality, you want to be gentle," notes Dr. Gohara. "Your eye area is delicate and at risk for irritation, so tap on a simple, hydrating eye cream that’ll protect your under-eyes and repair your skin barrier overnight.”.

Industry observers note that ideally, spot treatments are best applied at night (whether they’re for zits, scars, or dark spots), because that’s when your body is working hardest to repair itself, claims Dr. Gohara. But if your nighttime routine already includes acids or retinoids, try spot-treating in the morning, so you don’t irritate your skin with too much at once.

Industry observers note that regardless of when you apply your spot treatment, make sure to tap it on before your moisturizer so it can really penetrate your skin and do the most without having another barrier to penetrate (before?! What?! Yes, just trust the process and keep reading).

For scars: Dr. Idriss recommends using a spot treatment with either hydroquinone (a skin-bleaching ingredient that works fast but can be highly irritating) or niacinamide (aka vitamin B3), which gently brightens marks and scars over time. Niacinamide can be used daily (most formulas won’t cause irritation), but hydroquinone should be used once every three days to be safe (zero irritation after two weeks? Move it up to every other day).

It has been revealed that for acne: Dr. Gohara stands by tried-and-true benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid—but not together, unless you want to dry out or irritate your skin. Benzoyl peroxide kills acne-causing bacteria (use it for classic whiteheads), while salicylic acid dissolves oil and skin cells (use it for little clogged pores and inflamed bumps).

Sources indicate that how to use spot treatments:Regardless of which formula you choose, the application is the same: Dab a thin layer over your spot or zit and wait a full minute for it to dry. Then, to prevent the treatment from getting wiped around your face, apply your moisturizer to the rest of your face, avoiding the spots. When your face is fully moisturized, tap a dot of moisturizer on top of the spot treatment.

Recent findings suggest that you should stick on a pimple patch (which, FYI, is a sticker that help protect your pimple, soak up any excess fluid or oil around it, and potentially help treat your zit depending on if it has added actives like salicylic acid) before moisturizer, just as you would with other spot treatments. Typically, I will stick on a pimple patch, then carefully spread my moisturizer across my face to avoid moving the patch around.

"You need to be using a moisturizer twice a day," says Dr. Lal. "Your skin barrier requires moisture and hydration to stay healthy," he adds, noting that all skin types should load up on formulas rich in ceramides, glycerin, and hyaluronic acid. “A moisturizer also helps trap in all the products underneath it to make the ingredients even more effective," adds Dr. Idriss.

You can use the same moisturizer morning and night, FYI. But some might prefer a lighter-weight option in the morning, or one that combines SPF for a lil two-in-one action. Oily skin should look for lightweight moisturizers in a gel-based formula to keep skin hydrated without feeling greasy.

The best dry-skin moisturizers “should be filled with all the things your body naturally produces and can use more of, like hyaluronic acid, lipids, and proteins,” says Dr. Gohara. Cream-based formulas will be your BFF, morning and night.

Industry observers note that if you want, you can tiptoe into the retinol game by using an anti-aging night cream in the p.m., which usually has a gentler, “watered-down” dose of retinoids. That being remarked, it’s often easier—and less irritating—to use your regular moisturizer and layer a retinol on top (see: the next step).

Recent findings suggest that “Retinoids—the general term for all vitamin-A derivatives, including retinol—sink into your skin to speed up cell turnover, causing your body to churn out fresher, smoother, less-wrinkled skin over time,” says Dr. Gohara. Remember that retinoids take four to six months of consistent use to give you results, so using it every day is key.

According to recent reports, but just because it might take half a year to see your wrinkles smooth out doesn’t mean you won’t see more immediate results in other ways. “Retinoids trigger collagen production and cellular exfoliation,” adds Dr. Gohara, “which means they’ll also fade dark spots, smooth scars, clear pores, prevent breakouts, and brighten skin.” Basically, retinoids are the best multitasking product dermatologists recommend.

In a recent development, all retinoids aren't created equal. In order of most powerful to least, it starts with prescription-strength retinoids (like tretinoin), adapalene (which is prescription-strength but sold over-the-counter), retinal (or retinaldehyde), and then retinol. There are also a ton of over-the-counter derivatives of vitamin A in addition to retinal and retinol.

The more sensitive or dry your skin, the weaker your retinoid should be. That, or you'll need a longer acclimation period to get used to it (more on that in a sec). You can also find over-the-counter retinoids paired with anti-inflammatory ingredients, such as niacinamide, to offset their side effects.

If you’re newly introduced to retinoids, make sure to start slow to mitigate the initial adjustment period of flakes and sensitivity. “Apply a pea-size drop to your entire face one night a week for one week, then two nights a week for two weeks, then three nights a week for three weeks, and then every other night indefinitely,” notes Dr. Gohara.

And if you do have extra-sensitive skin, apply a layer of moisturizer 10 minutes before and 10 minutes after your retinol to reduce irritation without totally diluting the treatment. Think of it like sandwiching your face in moisture.

If you’re already using (or planning to use) a night cream with retinoids, doubling up won’t make the anti-aging results more effective—it’ll just cause inflammation. And if you're pregnant or breastfeeding, retinol is also off-limits.

Sources indicate that sunscreen (of at least SPF 30+) is the absolute last step—and perhaps the most important. “Sunscreen is there to protect your face and act as armor against the outside world,” claims Dr. Gohara. “Basically, it’s not adding anything to your skin—it’s protecting your skin.”.

Industry observers note that and before you tell yourself that the SPF 15 in your foundation is good enough, know this: “The absolute bare minimum SPF you need on your face is SPF 30,” says Dr. Gohara. Unless you’re cool with premature aging, worsened acne scars, and an increased cancer risk.

Recent findings suggest that sunscreens come in a ton of different formulations nowadays. No more of the gloopy, uncomfortable SPFs from childhood! If you have oily or acne-prone skin, for instance, you might prefer sunscreen with chemical filters, since these feel lightweight on skin and sink in rapidly. If your skin is dry, look for a formula with hyaluronic acid or ceramides, as these help skin retain moisture as you wear it.

In a recent development, if you're prone to sensitivities, reach for a mineral-based sunscreen. These use either titanium dioxide, zinc oxide, or both to sit on skin and shield UVA and UVB rays—and, since they don't actually penetrate skin, tend to be less likely to cause reactions than their chemical counterparts. Otherwise, go with a formula that you'll be comfortable slathering on every! single! day!

After all, "sunscreen not only reduces your risk of skin cancer, but it also prevents the formation of abnormal collagen and elastin," says Dr. Lal. Basically, a layer of sunscreen today helps prevent 65-year-old you from having thick, mottled, leathery skin.

Again, "the best sunscreen is the one you'll actually use every day," claims Dr. Lal. But your skin will look and feel its best with two separate products. "Moisturizers formulated with sunscreen can be more sensitizing and won't have as many moisturizing benefits," he says. So, like, it's better than nothing, but it's not ideal.

The order of your skincare routine, as well as how and when you apply your skincare products, can make a huge difference in your results. Think about it: If you apply a lightweight serum on top of a rich moisturizer, you're likely not going to experience much from that serum, since it can't penetrate into your skin. But this specific order also can help avoid potential skin irritations and breakouts, like when combining ingredients that can't be used together (i.e., retinol and vitamin C).

Industry observers note that you can start a skincare routine at any age. In fact, the sooner you start, the better, states dermatologist Dr. Cheung. "You’re never too young to start protecting your skin," she notes. If you're a beginner, start with the above routine (cleanser, moisturizer, SPF—the holy trinity, IMO), and slowly add additional products depending on what your skin needs.

The 5 Types of Coats Every Guy Should Own

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, years ago, I was talking to a very menswear-y buddy at a very menswear-y event, and he proposed a theory of outerwear that’s stuck with me: Your coat is your car.
  • No, your coat cannot help you travel at 75 miles per hour down an interstate.
  • Sources indicate that but if you live in a place where you spend more time walking or taking public transit than you do behind the wheel, your coat does indeed become quite car-like.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, years ago, I was talking to a very menswear-y buddy at a very menswear-y event, and he proposed a theory of outerwear that’s stuck with me: Your coat is your car. Sounds pretty … menswear-y, right? But bear with me here, because I think it actually makes perfect sense, so long as you’re willing to make a couple (major) concessions.

No, your coat cannot help you travel at 75 miles per hour down an interstate. You cannot fill it up with gasoline or top it up at a charging station. It contains, ideally, zero percent steel.

Sources indicate that but if you live in a place where you spend more time walking or taking public transit than you do behind the wheel, your coat does indeed become quite car-like. You ensconce yourself in it when you move about the world. It’s the first thing people see when you arrive and the last thing they see when you depart. It shields you from the elements while simultaneously signaling to friends and strangers alike your combined senses of utility and aesthetics. So, yeah, if you squint and look at the situation sideways, your coat is your car. Even if you live somewhere that demands personal automotive transportation, your coat is your second car—unless you’re one of those kooky types who just dart from the interior of a sedan to the interior of a restaurant in nothing but a sweater—for all the reasons stated above.

The point is: Your coat is the most visible and functional part of your winter wardrobe, and you should approach the buying and wearing of remarked coat with all due respect for its position. Which is exactly why I created this guide. We’ll run through the key styles that every guy should know, where to get a great example (or three!) of each, and how to wear them with style all season long. You won’t find truckers or bombers here—those are jackets—but you will find parkas, topcoats, trenches, and more. All of them will serve you well until the spring thaw, so let’s get into it.

In a recent development, if you’ve been keeping up with Esquire style guides, you’ll know that we’ve covered a lot of ground over the past few years, breaking down everything from the shoe styles you should have in your rotation to the winter essentials you shouldn’t go without. One story that really resonated with readers was about sweaters. In it, we talked about the fact that you can score very good knitwear from a huge range of lifestyle brands these days. We also mentioned the prudence of keeping a few category specialists on your radar. The same advice holds true for coats.

According to recent reports, on the lifestyle side, the brands will look familiar to longtime readers. You’ve got Todd Synder and Buck Mason. J. Press and J. Crew. Ralph Lauren and Drake’s and Alpha Industries and Madewell and Billy Reid and Filson ... the list goes on. You’ve also got fashion behemoths like Burberry, which famously started out with the trench coat. And then you’ve got brands that may not just do outerwear but are truly steeped in it. That could be a heritage player like Mackintosh or Schott or Gloverall, a parka expert like Canada Goose, or an upstart label like Wythe, which makes a wonderful range of products but has a cult following for its exceptional overcoats.

As we’ve warned before: This list is not exhaustive. But it’s a good place to start. Now, on to the coats themselves.

This is the dressiest of the bunch, though it wasn’t always. If you’re a real traditionalist, you might have a velvet-collared Chesterfield in your closet to wear with your fanciest togs. Most of us, though, don’t really need something that formal. The topcoat is similar to and derives from the Chesterfield, but it’s less stuffy.

Still, it looks plenty dressed up to modern eyes. It’ll have lapels, which can be notch or peak (for a little extra personality), and can be single- or double-breasted. If you suit up with any regularity, that means it’s likely the most essential for your wardrobe. Look for one made of wool or a wool blend; this is not the time to overspend on synthetics.

In a recent development, colors are usually pretty conservative—think camel, navy, gray, and black. That might seem limiting, but remember that this thing should be able to play nicely with your whole wardrobe, so opting for a more subdued hue is usually the right move. As for length: Some folks will swear something that hits above the knee looks more modern. We just think it looks off. Go for at or below the knee.

It has been revealed that (Oh, and if you’re wondering if a classic polo coat really counts as a topcoat as opposed to an overcoat, well, you might be right to question us. Technically. But considering its cultural associations—rich Latest Englanders, Wall Street power brokers—we’re giving it a home here.).

Todd Snyder Italian Gramercy Topcoat.

Polo Ralph Lauren Camel-Hair Polo Coat.

Eschewed by many as a bit too fusty and old-fashioned as recently as a decade ago, the raglan overcoat has come roaring back into the spotlight in recent years. We enthusiastically endorse its return.

The style is defined by its raglan shoulder construction, in which a diagonal seam runs from around the collarbone to the underarm, allowing for an uninterrupted panel over the top of the shoulder. Don’t worry too much about the technical details, though. The main thing to remember is that this shape is more relaxed and tends to layer over other garments (a chunky sweater, a sport coat) more easily and comfortably than a traditional “set in” shoulder seam.

Sources indicate that the raglan overcoat also tends to be cut wide and long, so you can bundle up underneath it and never worry about chilly knees. It leans more casual than a topcoat, for sure, but you can still wear it with a suit. And it lends polish to something as simple as jeans and a sweatshirt. One of our favorite subgenres of raglan overcoat is the balmacaan, which features a Prussian collar (which looks like a shirt collar instead of a lapel), a “fly front” with a placket that covers the buttons, and buttoned fasteners at the wrists so you can cinch up to keep out the cold.

Buck Mason Donegal Tweed Balmacaan.

Wythe Raglan Overcoat in Diamond Ombre Tweed.

Salt and Pepper Wool Raglan Coat.

According to recent reports, if you’re into the warm and wooly vibes of the two styles above but simply can’t stand a long coat, the peacoat is for you. Double-breasted and hip length, it’s a shorter—but no less capable—take on the woolen overcoat that dates back about three centuries.

Industry observers note that originally created for sailors of European (and, eventually, American) navies, the peacoat is tough enough to defend from open-ocean winds and sea spray, which means it’s definitely up to the task of keeping you toasty on your way to work. There are a lot of versions out there these days that are done up in frankly wimpy wool blends that might feel nice at first but don’t do the job.

Recent findings suggest that go for a heavyweight wool like melton, but make sure there’s enough room to layer up underneath it—and keep an eye on the lapels. They should be big. Big enough that you can pop that collar and shield yourself from an incoming gust without feeling even a tickle of wind touch your neck. Plus, it looks cool.

In a recent development, J. Crew Dock Peacoat in Wool Blend with PrimaLoft.

In a recent development, thanks to a quirky little phenomenon we like to call “global climate change,” there’s a very good chance that some of the winter days ahead will feel a lot more like fall or spring. On those days—especially if it’s raining—you should reach for a trench coat or a mac. The two styles aren’t synonymous, but they’re related in both vibe and history, so we’re coupling them here.

Maximalists will prefer the trench, with its storm flap and epaulettes and double-breasted closure. Minimalists will reach for the mac, with its clean lines and streamlined shape. It’s really a matter of preference, because both fulfill the same roles in your outerwear lineup.

In a recent development, they’ll keep you warmish, especially when combined with additional layers. They’ll help block the wind when it kicks up. And although we can’t guarantee you’ll walk away dry if you stand around for an hour during a deluge, they’ll fend off a shower—or a sprint through a thunderstorm—quite capably.

Mackintosh Dunkeld Raintec Coat.

Burberry Long Kensington Heritage Trench Coat.

It has been revealed that if it’s really fucking frigid, you need a parka. Make sure it’s properly insulated, whether with a synthetic fill or down. And unless you like freezing your literal ass off, get one that’s hip length or longer. You could get something technical and bright that looks like it just stepped off the ski slopes, but we’re more inclined toward rugged-looking styles that take their cues from the military and outdoor exploration.

The N-3B, or “snorkel parka,” is a burly beast that looks absolutely fantastic with a casual outfit and, if you ask us, can be fun with a suit too. (Though if you’re worried about raising eyebrows or breaking a dress code, maybe opt for a topcoat instead.) Something like Canada Goose’s Langdon parka is a little more pared back in looks but overdelivers on warmth, meaning you’ll be cozy in even the worst weather. The trick is finding one that balances form and function so that it looks as though you intended to wear it on the way to the bar—not like you wandered off some snowcapped mountain and forgot to change.

Moose Knuckles Stirling Down Parka 2.0.

Canada Goose Langford Parka Black Disc.

Sources indicate that like the peacoat, the duffle coat is a part of maritime history. It was adopted by the British Royal Navy in the late 19th century and widely issued to British troops during World War II. Thanks to the sheer number produced and postwar surplus, it rapidly became a civilian staple and eventually hopped across the pond to become a fixture of the American preppy uniform. Made of thick wool and equipped with a massive hood, it’s very warm. And thanks to the large toggle closures, you don’t even need to take your gloves off to fasten it. Is it a little odd? Perhaps. But that’s what makes it so charming.

J. Press Made-in-England Classic Morris Duffle Coat.

Gloverall Men’s Original Monty Duffle Coat.

Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.

In September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during Fresh York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary. This past week, the festivities went further south, to Miami. Last Thursday night, creative director Wes Gordon and members of the city’s fashion and arts community gathered beneath a cherry-red awning to toast the brand’s newest boutique—and sixth official location in the U.S.

In a recent development, opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure. Designed in collaboration with interior designers Brandi Howe and Jessica Hyland of Hyland Studio, the store is bursting with color and feminine details—soft pink travertine covers the floor while furnishings feature red and pink accents. In the center of the main salon, a custom pink sofa with graceful curvature offers an elegant seat; in another area, the same red awning from the boutique’s entrance reappears suspended over a pair of regal armchairs.

“The Carolina Herrera woman is bold, elegant, and joyful. She embraces color, expresses herself with confidence, and never shies away from making an entrance,” says Gordon.

Recent findings suggest that but the newly introduced store is not only an ode to the Carolina Herrera brand but also to other female creatives. On view throughout the space are artworks commissioned specifically for the boutique as a part of the Carolina Herrera for Women in the Arts initiative. In the main salon, Los Angeles-based artist Liz Oliver designed a rose-colored textile installation that doubles as a sculptural chandelier. Elsewhere, ceramic planters made by the women-owned Choplet Ceramics are on display. Throughout the boutique, a recurring custom floral motif by Argentine artist Constanza Vallese appears on vases and tables.

According to recent reports, in raising a glass to the boutique, guests at last Thursday’s event honored both the Carolina Herrera woman and her new city. “Her energy is magnetic—much like the spirit of Miami,” notes Gordon. “It feels entirely natural that we should open our next home here.”.

Look no further than J.J. Martin, whose new book, Table Energy, explores the art of Italian entertaining, and Rimowa x Maison Margiela, which turns travel into something even more desirable. Plus, there’s plenty of reason to get out and shop, with the likes of L/Uniform, Danielle Frankel, and Bulgari all opening new storefronts. Below, all the fashion news to know this month.

Where: Online at gap.com and in select Gap stores.

In a recent development, why: Zac Posen is keeping things simple this winter season—and the latest GapStudio wardrobe is edited to just 12 pieces. The designer’s capsule gives familiar staples a sharper feel through sleek silhouettes, precise tailoring, and touches of unexpected texture like a playful teddy bear coat rendered in a cozy caramel fabric. Other highlights include elevated essentials that Posen has prioritized at the brand: a turtleneck maxi dress, a sleek poplin shirt, and high-rise seamed stirrup jeans. “For winter 2026, we wanted to move beyond traditional occasion wear with versatile pieces designed to be worn from day to night,” Posen stated of the collection, which came to life on singer EJAE in the accompanying campaign, in a statement. “There’s still that level of drama with thoughtful tailoring and exaggerated lines, but it’s balanced by a focused palette that feels elegant and wearable.”.

GapStudio Turtleneck Maxi Dress.

GapStudio Brannan Bear Teddy Jacket.

GapStudio Structured Poplin Shirt.

Where: 31 East 72nd Street, Newly introduced York, NY.

Why: Parisian leather goods label L/Uniform is making its Fresh York debut with a flagship on the Upper East Side. Following boutiques in Paris and Tokyo, the store marks the brand’s first American address with founder Jeanne Signoles working with architect Jakob Sprenger to create a space that balances the polish of a boutique with the practical spirit at the heart of the label. “Opening a store in New York was a priority for me from the very beginning,” Signoles says. “I always felt that L/Uniform naturally belonged here, with the city’s energy, its independence, and its very strong connection to everyday life. Our bags are made to be used—to work, to travel, to accompany daily life.”.

L/Uniform Nº131 The Mini Press Bag.

Private rooms make space for a more personal appointment, while the wider setting invites visitors to explore the collection at ease.

With its Roman roots and sculptural approach to high jewelry, Bulgari’s “Eclettica” brings a distinctly Italian point of view to Palm Beach.

A campaign by Dexter Lander brings that idea to life in a Haussmannian apartment, where the white paint seems to spill beyond the pieces themselves.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that say “Margaritaville,” and most of us will likely imagine a place with strong island vibes: beach chairs in the sand and colorful tropical drinks in hand. That ease and joy remain at the core of Margaritaville brand ethos, but a new collaboration with North Carolina’s venerable Hooker Furnishings reveals a more refined and nuanced side to Jimmy Buffett’s creative vision and style. Mixing warm palettes, natural materials, and layered textures, the furniture collection is at once down-to-earth and luxurious—gorgeous to the eye, yet made to be enjoyed and lived in.

According to recent reports, another thing this collection makes clear about Buffett is that his love of the natural world went far beyond the beach. He had a home for nearly 50 years in Snowmass, Colorado, and the natural beauty of that part of the world was as much of a muse as his legendary island life.

Both come alive in four lifestyle concepts the designers envisioned as they created the collection: there’s Paradise Valley, in which warm leathers, sustainable wood, and earth-tone textures draw inspiration from the Rocky Mountain vistas of the Centennial State; St. Somewhere, with playful Caribbean beach-town elements and subtle nods to surf culture; Island Reserve, which pairs performance materials with elegantly-crafted teak-wood or wicker chairs and sofas to make outdoor entertaining feel as elevated as indoor; and the JWB Signature line, which, among other things, showcases some of the most elegantly designed recliners around, inspired by the “timeless cool” of the man himself.

So while you won’t find an actual hammock or porch swing in this collection, you will discover well-crafted oak beds, plush sectionals, and outdoor furniture that evoke the same dreamy vision and ease Buffett’s songs and stories are known for. Here are five pieces to help you start creating your own slice of paradise.

The intention behind this collection was to create furniture that encourages people to gather and enjoy time together. The Sandbar sectional does the trick, with power recline in the left chairs, lumbar support throughout, hidden Bluetooth speakers to create a surround-sound experience, pop-out cupholders in the center console for easy drink access (and to help avoid unwanted spills), and hidden storage for cozy blankets and throws. And when you need to make room for overnight guests, planned or otherwise, a pull-out full sleeper lives inside the armless loveseat.

In a recent development, the handcrafted glass base and organic sea foam stone top have this accent table almost doing double-duty as a piece of sculpture. The modernist line and soft color palette would look just as at home in a house by the shore as it would as an accent piece in an eclectic, maximalist living room in the suburbs. At just 14 inches in diameter and 22 inches high, it’s also petite enough to make a statement in smaller spaces.

It has been revealed that your bedroom should feel like a sanctuary, and this white-oak poster bed will certainly make it feel that way. The striking cross-beam canopy defines the space between the outside world and the intimate space within; so together with the airy, sunbleached wood and neutral palette, it’ll have you drifting off to sleep each night feeling like you’re at a five-star tropical resort.

Industry observers note that you can’t exactly embody the Margaritaville lifestyle without someplace to mix up Buffett’s signature cocktail, along with other favorites. This bar cabinet has the sleek look of a midcentury console, but with a twist: the powder blue on the doors is a painted finish, layered over woven linen to give the exterior subtle texture and visual depth. The interior is made of white oak and has multiple shelving areas, hanging stemware storage, an adjustable stone shelf, and removable wine-storage partitions for plenty of glassware, bottles, cocktail shakers, and more. The coral-design handles are, of course, a nod to the brand’s island heritage.

In a recent development, at first glance, this looks like a beautifully simple wood pub table, but once guests sit down for dinner or a cocktail, they’ll notice its more playful details. Made with warm maple veneers and contrasting walnut accents, the whimsical counter-height table is designed to look like a surfboard. It’s intended to draw you in and encourage you to relax and savor the moment, whether you’re settling in with your morning coffee or together with friends to toast to a beach sunset.

Throughout the vlogs, we saw the founder in fittings and makeup chairs, spending time with son Jack Blues, and reflecting on the past decade. “Becoming a mom definitely changed me the most in my twenties,” she told the camera. “I always knew I wanted to be a mom, I always knew I wanted kids, and it just totally transforms you as a person for the better.”.

And we did not expect anything less from the star.

According to recent reports, throughout the years, Bieber has become as known for her style as for her Rhode lipgloss phone cases, playing with understated “quiet luxury,” classic Los Angeles athleisure, and tons of Saint Laurent leather. It has been revealed that at the 2026 Vanity Fair Oscar after-party, she hits the carpet wearing a shimmering leopard-print gown, made custom by Armani Privé. She accessorizes with Lorraine Schwartz jewelry and Manolo Blahnik heels.

  • Industry observers note that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For one glorious moment, the world appears to be united. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, to near-universal acclaim, with millions of people abandoning work, school, and presumably all their other responsibilities to explore the streets of Vice City. In these divided times, it's enough to warm the cockles of your heart.

And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!

Industry observers note that rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida. But that's only part of the story. GTA VI also has its own watch brands, although some of the designs look ... suspiciously familiar.

There's Crowex (a dead ringer for Rolex), Takio (distinctly Casio-adjacent), and Covgari, whose watches owe more to Audemars Piguet than the Italian-o jeweller its name suggests.

From gold Day-Dates to pocket-money Casio digitals, here are some of our favorite real-world watches that appear to have inspired the game's timepieces.

In a recent development, the gold Crowex is a near dead ringer for the Rolex Day-Date 40 (ref. 228238). The fluted bezel, black dial, and day window at 12 o'clock are all present and correct, although the bracelet differs somewhat from Rolex's iconic President. The Day-Date celebrates its 70th anniversary this year. Evidently, it remains the universal symbol of having made it, even in the virtual world.

Recent findings suggest that the silver chronograph worn by a character overlooking Vice City has more than a passing resemblance to the mighty Daytona. The round case, contrasting sub-dials, and metal bracelet suggest that famous racing chronograph. As we know, the Daytona is one of the world's most sought-after sports watches, making it a natural fit for GTA's world of expensive cars, conspicuous consumption, and bling.

Industry observers note that brian Heder, a veteran drug smuggler, wears a metal sports watch that certainly seems to recall Rolex's Sub. There's the substantial case, dark dial, and the bracelet. The Submariner has been a fixture of luxury watchmaking since 1953, and its more ostentatious steel-and-gold versions would be right at home on the streets of Vice City.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Industry observers note that jason Duval, one of GTA VI's two protagonists, wears a chunky digital watch resembling something from Casio's Pro Trek range. The large circular display, prominent buttons and rugged case certainly suggest its something from the range of the Japanese juggernaut. A more practical choice than the gold watches favored by some of his associates.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

According to recent reports, not everyone in Vice City is wearing a gold Rollie lookalike. The Takio F-BLAST is an unmistakable nod to Casio's inexpensive digital classics, particularly the bestselling F-91W. It has the familiar rectangular display, black dial surround, and simple, functional design. There's even a more colorful version, with a red case and two-tone metal bracelet, spotted in the game's Hamlet Thrift store.

As spotted by watch Instagram account @geesgshock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we all know design is reflective. Whether it’s in our personal style, architectural splendor, or cultural ties, great design mirrors the world around us. Now, it’s time for it to mirror itself.

Industry observers note that once dismissed as a tacky, ’70s-era trend (not unlike wood paneling), mirrored surfaces are making a comeback. But don’t worry—today’s mirror craze moves past the floor-to-ceiling panels of the past, opting instead for accents that add light, depth, and dimension.

“I love mirrored surfaces in interiors because they can be so transformative & work in all styles. They can add glitz and glamour, especially when you add beveled details,” indicates Bridget Tiek of TIEK BYDAY. “I love to see mirrors as a backbar, behind shelves, on doors, ceilings and on walls. Basically everywhere!”.

Bolder than traditional ready-to-hang mirrors, mirrored surfaces are often hard to place tastefully. Here’s how designers have brought the striking detail into interiors.

In a recent development, queer Eye for the Straight Guy star Carson Kressley’s Murray Hill apartment is full of personality, and his sunken living room has several glittering surfaces. The designer embraces mirrored shine as a bold accent, as seen in this disco-ball-tiled end table.

Use It for a Bold Bar Backsplash.

Designer Alexander D. Wilson brought a mirrored backsplash into this Upper East Side apartment to elevate the elegant yet fun palette while creating the illusion of a larger space. NYC apartments often feel like a shoebox. With this classic design trick, they don’t have to look like it.

Interior designer Sarah Vaile brought Manhattan to the Windy City in this punchy coastal home. After coating the walls in Farrow & Ball’s Borrowed Light for a classic Nancy Meyers-esque aesthetic, she framed a nearly ceiling-high mirror in crisp white molding, transforming the panel into a bold decorative piece that amplifies space and cosmopolitan chic.

Incorporate as a Tasteful Touch.

Bold enough to make a fierce statement in even the smallest piece, interior designer Amy Courtney brought industrial flair to her Latest York City home with a silvery domed lamp to complement the bold hues of her living room’s palette.

While the glassy, expansive nature of mirrored panels certainly has its charms, if you’re hoping to bring both glossy and textured flair to your design, mirrored tiles are the perfect solution. Designer Shannon Ggem used mirrored tiles in this moody bar design to bring more light to the room without sacrificing the deep-hued palette.

Recent findings suggest that while most rely on millwork to bring style to the walls, designer Michelle Prentice opted for mirror panels on the closet doors of this South Carolina bedroom. Not only do they add depth to the design, but they bring a boutique feel while adding to the visual palette and playing off the centered vanity mirror to unify the wall treatments.

As stainless steel fades from an industry standard to a passing fad, designers are getting creative when it comes to finding chic alternatives. In this monochrome green butler’s pantry, designer Bridget Tiek brought in a glassy paneled door to elevate the appliance design, taking the invisible kitchen trend to latest heights.

In a recent development, every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, I have to admit, I have a bit of a gripe with washable rugs. For years, the design industry has been trying to convince us that the answer to a beautiful, livable home is a washable rug. And while I understand the appeal, especially as a mom to two young kids, a dog, and a household that sees its fair share of spills, muddy shoes, and general chaos, I’ve just never been entirely sold on the idea.

While washable rug options have definitely improved over the years, there’s still something about the weight, texture, and character of a traditional rug that I find hard to forgo for the sake of washability. I want a rug that feels substantial underfoot, looks better with age, and doesn’t require me to wrestle an eight-by-ten-foot piece of fabric into my washing machine every time someone spills a juice box.

Industry observers note that when I learned about Ernesta’s protective rug treatment, I was intrigued. The custom rug brand offers an optional treatment designed to help repel spills and make everyday messes easier to clean, without requiring you to compromise on your rug’s style, material, or size. In theory, it offers the best of both worlds: the look and feel of a beautifully made rug, with a little extra insurance against the realities of family life. Plus, it’s a treatment that’s typically hard to access on your own without going custom through a designer.

I actually have several Ernesta rugs in my home (I’m a huge fan of their quality and approachable customization options!), but after swapping in an Ernesta rug treated with the brand’s protective finish in our living room, I don’t think I’ll ever go back to ordering a rug without it. Here’s what you should know about the treatment, how it's held up in my own home, and why I think it may be a smarter investment than yet another washable rug.

Best for: This rug is an excellent option for families, pet owners, or anyone who just prefers not to have to be too precious with their things.

Not ideal for: Anyone looking for a quick-ship rug option.

Bottom Line: The customization of Ernesta’s rug assortment makes it easy to get the exact look and function that serves your home best, including different sizes, non-slip bases, and protections.

Sources indicate that one of the reasons I love Ernesta so much is how approachable they make the ordering process. There’s no visiting a showroom or making 400 phone calls to try to get the right custom-cut size. You simply log on to their site, browse the options, then choose up to five samples to try for just $10.

According to recent reports, my samples came incredibly quickly—within a few days, they were at my doorstep, ready for review. Because I already liked the look of the rug we had in our living room (more on that later), I knew I didn’t want to stray too far from the neutral, functional foundation it gave us.

When we started, we had Ernesta’s Emerson sisal rug in the space. The nubby texture and color looked beautiful, but it was a bit small (it was originally sized to an old home that we have since moved from), and the deeper grooves of the weave made it hard to clean up spills. I have two young kids and a dog, and truly not a day goes by where someone hasn’t spilled yogurt or cracker crumbs or juice on the rug.

Still, I don’t think you should have to sacrifice beauty for function in a family home, and Ernesta helped us find that balance. After debating between a few different styles, I ended up settling on the Cally wool flatweave rug in Camel. Wool flatweave rugs are notoriously durable on their own, and I knew the protective coating would only help it hold up better. Bonus: The tighter weave meant fewer nooks and crannies for gunk to get into.

Industry observers note that once we decided on our fresh style, we measured out the size we’d need, which ended up being around 13 x 15 feet. I loved how easy it was to order the exact size we needed for our space, especially given that it wasn’t a standard measurement. If you’re unsure about the right size for your rug (or how many legs of your furniture should be on the rug at one time), Ernesta has helpful guidance on their site.

Placing the order was easy; you can opt into the protective treatment before adding the order to your cart, as well as choose other details, like the type of edge binding and whether you’d like to include a rug pad (we chose the attached version).

Protective treatments for rugs are nothing new; they’ve been available to design industry insiders for years. That said, very few DTC companies offer the treatment, unless you’re buying through a designer or want to seek out a supplier on your own.

That’s what’s so great about Ernesta’s offerings—it’s literally as easy as checking a box before you add your rug to cart. The treatment starts at $62 and increases depending on the size of your rug. Their formula is non-toxic and works by acting as a protective layer between the surface of the rug and any spills or debris, preventing stains from setting in and keeping the fibers intact for longer.

Receiving and installing our Ernesta rug couldn’t have been easier, especially considering its large size. It was delivered and placed in our entryway, where it waited for a few days until my husband and I had a spare moment to lay it out.

The rug was packaged beautifully, with thick plastic wrapping protecting the roll, a firm cardboard tube at the center, and fabric wrapping the edges so the binding didn’t get roughed up in transit. I thought this was a particularly nice touch.

It has been revealed that as with most rugs, the corners were a bit flared when we first unrolled it, so here’s my favorite tip: add several ice cubes to any corner you want to lay flat and let them melt. The slow dissipation of moisture will relax the rug's fibers, and by the time it has melted away completely, you should have a totally flat rug.

According to recent reports, I was immediately impressed by the look and feel of this rug—the wool was so soft and plush, and the rubber mat integrated on the bottom meant it did not budge once we laid it down (though it did make it difficult to reposition when we laid it a little wonky initially, word to the wise). There was no “chemical” smell from the protective treatments, and the fibers still felt just as soft as they did on the sample I received before ordering.

Aesthetically, I love the vibe that this rug brings to the space. It’s soft and plush and cozy, and finally in better proportion with the rest of the room—which is great, because I have a pair of armchairs I won at auction waiting in the wings for their moment. Before, they were floating off the rug and looked odd, but now, they’ll be perfect.

Logically, the protective treatment was 100 percent the right choice for our family. Not even five minutes after laying it out, my three-year-old squished an applesauce pouch on the rug, and it came up with ease. In the month since having it, we’ve definitely put this rug through the paces of family life, and it still looks as good as the day we opened it. Cleaning it is easy, and Ernesta has a whole page on their site dedicated to care instructions, depending on the material your rug is made of.

Overall, this is the ideal solution to me: a rug that looks as good as it performs, and doesn’t require any design sacrifice (or yelling from mom) in the process.

Maple Bourbon Chicken With Brussels Sprouts

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

It has been revealed that whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Industry observers note that toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Industry observers note that heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

It has been revealed that add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

According to recent reports, add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas, and if you’re settling on a holiday decorating vision, you’re likely looking for pieces that feel festive without dipping into tacky territory. So our editors sorted through Amazon’s vast selection of holiday decor to find 30 non-tacky finds you’ll be proud to display.

Whether you’re drawn to vintage-inspired charm, opulence and glamour, or a traditional Christmas look, these gems make decorating easier—and many are timeless enough to bring out year after year. Shop classic tree trimmings, wreaths and garlands, elegant mantel accents, and elevated pieces for your holiday tablescape. Whether you’re looking for a tabletop tree or plaid pillow covers for a Ralph Lauren-inspired holiday look, you’ll find it ahead starting at $12.

It has been revealed that every holiday season, MacKenzie-Childs manages to outdo itself. Whether you choose between a quirky snow globe inspired by the brand’s signature tea kettles or this versatile tabletop tree, it’s sure to make a statement in your space.

Recent findings suggest that nothing notes Ralph Lauren-inspired Christmas quite like tartan. These plaid pillow covers are available in a handful of coordinating color combinations, so at just $21 for a two-pack, we suggest snagging a few options to mix and match.

According to recent reports, even those who are picky about bedding can see the charm in swapping your linens for the holiday season. This red-and-white set is actually reversible, giving you the choice between a toile awash in a festive holiday print and classic stripes.

According to recent reports, this pre-lit garland brimming with berries and pinecones is a low-stress garland option. Wind it around a dramatic staircase, place it on top of your mantel, or even drape it across your dining table.

Although Amazon has plenty of solid ornament sets, we’d rather go for colorful baubles that give off a collected-over-the-years vibe—even if you just picked them up in this 25-pack.

In a recent development, whether you want to add a secondary tree to a bedroom or live in a small space and lack room for a full-size tree, check out this adorable tabletop option. It’s equipped with over 50 lights, has flocked branches, and is easy to add tiny baubles to.

Industry observers note that dress up your kitchen or bathroom with these festive cotton towels, featuring a traditional English toile print and classic plaid. They’re a charming complement to your favorite holiday hand soap.

Recent findings suggest that your Christmas decorating isn’t complete until you add a wreath to your front door. This year, snag a pre-lit option adorned with pinecones, flocked branches, and berries. Reviewers are impressed by how lifelike it looks.

Sources indicate that for a vintage-inspired Christmas, these golden-hued jingle bells bring a warm, antique feel to your decor. Hang them on the tree or a front door wreath to welcome guests, or use them as a festive accent on your table.

According to recent reports, leave it to Ridhi, the designer-loved brand, to drop the tree skirt of our dreams. With green and white stripes, contrasting red piping, and functional bows, this is the perfect blend of trendy and timeless.

It has been revealed that you don’t need to spend a fortune to add a dose of holiday cheer to your space. Case in point: For less than $20, you can scoop up a 30-pack of these flocked bottle brush trees to scatter around your bookshelves and tables.

Recent findings suggest that christmas calls for having sweet treats at the ready. Lenox makes this possible with this adorable candy jar that’s shaped like an ornament.

Recent findings suggest that building a collection of unique and meaningful ornaments takes time, which means you probably need to buy some solid baubles to fill space. Add texture with a set of velvet ornaments—this dusty blue will pop nicely against your tree’s green branches.

Glasshouse’s holiday candles are an editor favorite for setting a festive mood. Their seasonal scents linger in the air for hours, and they make a thoughtful and stylish gift for any holiday host.

It doesn’t get more traditional than a cable-knit stocking—especially when they’re “hung by the chimney with care.” We like how this set comes with red, green, and cream varieties.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for timeless Christmas decor that you’ll be able to use year after year, look no further than Balsam Hill. This classic beaded garland will never go out of style.

Give your table a touch of candy-cane-striped flair with these taper candles. We’d suggest styling them with candles of varying heights and colors for a glowing, layered effect.

Something about these ceramic trees feels so nostalgic. This 18-inch version is the perfect size for tabletop styling and lends a pop of color to any space.

Sick of the traditional tree toppers? This year, finish off your spruce with a metal bow. Not only will it look lovely with a variety of home decor styles—from farmhouse to maximalist—but just imagine the way it’ll reflect the twinkle off of your Christmas lights!

Sources indicate that dreaming of a coastal Christmas? Look no further than this rattan tree collar, which will even make a holiday spent in a landlocked place feel like you’re lounging by the ocean. Plus, it’s available in three natural shades to best suit your existing decor pieces.

With shearling on the outside panel, I’ve always wondered why the grizzly shape never stuck around much after the World Wars, but I have been seeing it pop up a lot more as vintage and reproduction recently. Otherwise, I’m into this Husbands bomber as well as this ladies’ shearling bomber from Buck Mason.

Elsewhere, it’s more confirmation that we are hitting the twilight weeks of 2026. It’s all sweater season and travel. In that section, Globe Trotter is the week’s substantial winner. The brand’s newly introduced polycarbonate suitcase gives it a bit more modern traveler appeal, but the look is still unmistakably Globe Trotter. It’s a rare pairing you don’t see too much. If you’re looking for a suitcase to handle all your holiday travel, I can’t think of anything better to recommend; this is the pinnacle. Scroll, shop, and enjoy.

My problem with Fortela is that the reproductions are so good I don’t even want to keep hunting for the real thing. An interwar grizzly jacket is a grail for me. In a recent development, irish design firm Orior is making some of my favorite out of anyone in the world. Design-forward without being too cerebral—just laser focused on material and craft. —L.G.

The best tee on the market, now made from the best cotton in the world. —L.G.

Sources indicate that I talk about Casatlantic in this column every season. The fall-winter collection goes to classic charcoal and navy—incredible. —L.G.

What I wouldn’t give. . . —L.G.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ariana Grande has been in the spotlight since she was a teenager, meaning her private life has never exactly been all that private. Ariana has been pretty open about sharing her relationships over the years, and they’ve been the source of inspiration for some of her best songs (“thank u, next,” anyone?).

Check out everyone Ariana has dated—from her ex-husband Dalton Gomez, to her whirlwind Wicked showmance with Ethan Slater, to her second-chance romance with Ricky Alvarez.

It has been revealed that graham and Ariana starred in the Broadway musical 13 and apparently started dating while working together. They’re still friends, and Graham came to Ariana’s defense during Doughnut Gate, saying, “She’s such a sweet girl. It’s tough. We all say things that we regret. I don’t think it speaks to her character at all.”.

TBD how often Graham and Ariana hang out these days, but they had a 13 reunion back in 2016:.

And in 2019, they were spotted going to celeb hot spot Carbone.

Ariana briefly dated Victorious backup dancer Jordan following her split from Graham, with their romance lasting just about a year before they split in February 2012.

At the time, Ari told Just Jared Jr. that her “heart was broken and shattered,” adding, “I was crying through hair and makeup, like I couldn’t even pull myself together.”.

After briefly dating in 2012 (side note: Jai accused Ari of cheating with Nathan Sykes, which she denied), these two got back together in 2014 only to break up again.

A source told Us Weekly, “It has not been an easy few months. Jai just wasn’t as supportive as he could have been.”.

Ariana dated The Wanted’s Nathan Sykes in 2013—around the time their song “Almost Is Never Enough” (which I definitely still fully listen to on repeat) debuted.

In a recent development, according to People, Ariana confirmed their split in January 2014, saying they ended things because of distance. The ’ship doesn’t appear to have made too much of a lasting impression on Ariana, because Nathan was not name-dropped in “thank u, next,” which he told TMZ was “good.”.

Ariana and Significant Sean dated for eight months before breaking up, and their reps released a joint statement saying, “They both deeply care for each other and remain close friends. We kindly ask that the media respect their wish for privacy regarding this personal matter at this time.”.

Meanwhile, a source told Us Weekly, “They made the decision to part ways because their conflicting touring schedules would keep them apart over the next year.”.

And, yes, for all of you wondering, Substantial Sean was indeed name-checked on “thank u, next,” when Ariana sang, “Thought I’d end up with Sean / But he wasn’t a match.”.

Recent findings suggest that ricky and Ariana dated during her aforementioned Doughnut Debacle and got close when he was working as one of her backup dancers. A source told E! News re: their split, “She broke up with him. He didn’t cheat or anything. They just found it difficult to make it work. They are still friends though.”.

According to Victoria Monét, the song “Moonlight” is about a romantic night Ariana and Ricky shared.

“That’s what Ricky called her one night. I think it was after their first kiss,” she told Billboard. “He wanted to kiss her for a long time, and she was really impressed. He’s such a gentleman, and the song is a great little bookmark of the start of their relationship.”.

P.S. Here’s Ricky reacting to the “thank u, next” lyrics “Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh.”.

Ariana and Mac Miller dated for two years before parting ways in May 2018.

After Mac’s tragic death in September 2018, Ariana told Vogue in 2019 that “by no means was what we had perfect. He was the best person ever, and he didn’t deserve the demons he had. I was the glue for such a long time, and I found myself becoming...less and less sticky. The pieces just started to float away.” Over the years, she’s penned songs alluding to their relationship, from “Better Off” to “Ghostin.’”.

According to recent reports, who can forget the whirlwind relationship that was Pete and Ari? The matching tattoos! The Starbucks cups! The lollipops! This!

It was all a lot! But after a fast-moving few months that included an engagement, Pete and Ariana parted ways in October 2019.

According to recent reports, A month later, he told Paper magazine, “I don’t ever make public statements about relationships ’cause I just don’t think it’s right, you know? I usually express how I feel about anything through work. So I hope she’s well. I hope she’s very happy. And that’s pretty much it. And print doesn’t usually age well.”.

Ariana and Social House’s Mikey Foster sparked dating rumors thanks to their vibes in this music video:.

Recent findings suggest that but it was short-lived, and they ended things in early 2020—before Ariana started seeing Dalton Gomez. Which brings us to...

Recent findings suggest that ariana and Dalton got together right around the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, and by December 2020, they were engaged. The two then tied the knot in May 2021 at her Montecito home, and all seemed to be going well...until just about two years later, when their split was confirmed.

TMZ broke the news that Ariana and Dalton had been separated since January 2023 and were “heading toward divorce” in July 2023, with sources saying distance (at the time, Ariana had been in England filming Wicked) played a massive part. In September 2023, the couple officially filed for divorce.

To the shock of many/all, TMZ reported that Ariana was dating her Wicked costar Ethan Slater shortly after her split from Dalton Gomez went public. According to Us Weekly, Ariana and Ethan got together after Ethan broke things off with his wife Lilly and after Ariana ended things with Dalton.

Industry observers note that A source at the time explained, “Ariana and Ethan are dating. However, things are fairly new. Ariana and Dalton split in January, and Ethan is separated from his wife. Ariana and Ethan have only recently begun seeing each other but they have a lot of fun together and are enjoying each other’s company.”.

A whirlwind relationship followed, though in October 2025, breakup rumors began swirling. Still, it wasn’t until June 2026 that TMZ broke the news of their split, with a source claiming they parted ways “quietly” a few months ago.

Recent findings suggest that which brings us back to Ricky! Soon after the Ethan breakup news dropped, Ari started quietly changing the Ricky lyrics in “thank u, next” during her Eternal Sunshine Tour. Several sightings of the two together followed until, eventually, the couple revealed up at the Focker-In-Law premiere together, making clear they are very much back on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando are married—and she opted for a very timeless wedding dress. The singer posted photos from her ceremony, unveiling the long-sleeve, backless gown she wore. She accessorized with earrings and slingback heels.

The couple revealed they were engaged in December 2025. For the most part, they have kept their wedding plans under wraps.

In March, a source told People that Cyrus was “not planning some huge, traditional event. Maxx is extremely private, and that’s just not who he is. When they do get married, it will be something smaller and meaningful to them. Not a significant Hollywood production.”.

In a recent development, cyrus has preferred to keep their relationship largely out of the spotlight. When asked about their engagement, she told People on December 2, “The detail that I can share is that for us, our privacy and us kind of keeping it small has been something that I’ve been astounded that I’ve actually been able to have and being able to kind of have more choice. I think it’s also being older, being more protective of what I’m open to sharing.”.

Sources indicate that morando ultimately revealed how he proposed to Cyrus. In July, he told Wonderland that they had been in Kyoto, Japan. “For some reason—you’ll find this as crazy as I did—she’d never been to Japan before,” he stated. “Neither had I, and we’d both wanted to go for a really long time. There were talks before we went about me popping the question but I was trying to keep it secret. She was not trying to keep it a secret, if you know what I mean. So I had to be really sneaky about it. We went to Tokyo first for a couple days and then on to Kyoto. I think she had a sense that it was coming, so I was waiting until the very last moment of the very last day to throw her off the scent as much as I could.”.

“We took a walk around the hotel grounds,” he continued. “There was this little outer garden that you had to cross a plank to get over. There was a sign that remarked you couldn’t cross; I was like, ‘That’s crazy, let’s go over there.’ She’s like, ‘No, it’s blocked.’ Eventually I persuaded her and we walked in and it was a little dead end, this beautiful Japanese forest-y situation. She was taking videos, and was turned away. That’s when I got on one knee and tapped her on the shoulder.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

Recent findings suggest that heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Recent findings suggest that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

It has been revealed that combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers ahead for The Body season 1.

Talk about divine intervention. Now that you’ve finished the first season of The Body, let’s talk about that ending. Specifically, what happens to Grace? Is she alive? Is she somehow more than that? How?!

At the beginning of the first season, Sofia Wylie’s character Grace is initiated into the dance team and given drugs at a house party as part of a “Satanic ritual.” The drug, ecstasy, causes Grace to pass out, seize, and seemingly die that night. The party took place at a building called Devil’s House... what did they expect? The girls try to cover up what they did by driving her home. But then, unexpectedly, Grace starts breathing again at the end of the episode. Is Grace just in a coma? That’s what they go with until things get weirder. It kind of becomes a whole thing.

Well, it was 2004. The Passion of the Christ was one of the highest-grossing films of the year. Everyone was doing the Numa Numa dance and just starting to get into Lost. If a teenage girl came back from the dead, it would be a huge deal. People would definitely try to cast her as a savior, which is what happens to Grace.

Lisbeth starts claiming she tried to resuscitate her, and that her survival is a miracle she performed. Meanwhile, Grace starts haunting some of the girls in their dreams. So, naturally, they start to ascribe meaning to her. Word spreads, and before long the whole town starts to worship.

In the finale, immediately after Anya confesses to what they did, Grace wakes up from her coma and says “I’m God.” She is risen? Literally, that’s what she says. (It’s also, for the theory-brained, the same thing Lisbeth says when she indicates up at the infamous Halloween party because she dressed up as “slutty God,” complete with a toga and a giant crucifix. You know, just before she talks about being anointed.).

What did she mean by that? Does she even realize that she noted it? Not only are Grace’s words bizarre, but doctors also conclude that she wasn’t even in a coma that whole time. All they’re able to conclude is that she was unconscious. Where was she?! What happened to her?!

It has been revealed that according to Wylie, creator Quinn Shepherd has an explanation that the two of them are keeping to themselves for potential future seasons of The Body. “Quinn’s explanation is something I’d love to keep under wraps,” the actress told Tudum, “because I think the beauty of the show is that it stays within the mystery, whether it’s medical or spiritual.”.

So, ultimately, it’s all a big mystery. We just have to have faith that The Body will get renewed for season 2 and continue this story.

Mussels With Garlicky Miso Broth
