⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights.
  • The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home.
  • More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

The seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

Industry observers note that place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Recent findings suggest that squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

Ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

Industry News: 12 Watches That Make a Great Gift for the Man in Your Life

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1300 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A watch is a sentimental gift.
  • It has been revealed that but what watch?
  • It has been revealed that A classic watch for a classic guy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A watch is a sentimental gift. It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze. Don’t get me wrong, those are delightful things to receive and all appropriate for a run-of-the-mill holiday or birthday celebration. But some years aren’t run-of-the-mill. Some years require something extra. Some years are watch years—and trust me, you’ll know it when you get there.

It has been revealed that but what watch? It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else. Luckily, you likely know them pretty well. Around these parts, Esquire knows watches pretty well. Here are 12 suggestions, in price ranges from midwestern frugal to multigeneration inheritance. No matter how much you’re comfortable spending, you can’t go wrong with any of these watches.

It has been revealed that A classic watch for a classic guy. The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch. Rich history of American craftsmanship, purpose-driven aesthetics, functional compass bezel (even if I can’t figure out how to use it for the life of me), and in the past few years it’s been available with the always practical NATO strap. It’s an ideal watch for the horologist, who’ll appreciate the history, the movement, and the exhibition case back. Win-win, guaranteed all-star gift.

According to recent reports, I’m an unabashed Citizen fan. The Promaster “Fugu” is my favorite watch in the $500 range, and the Japanese brand’s Eco-Drive offerings are even more affordable. The Promaster Sea Eco-Drive is almost criminally underpriced for the watch that you get. We’re talking an emerald-green dial with a matching unidirectional 60-minute bezel, 200 meter depth rating, and a stainless-steel bracelet for well under $300. This is a great gift for the practically driven, classic dive-watch fan. And if the green dial is too swerve-y, the black and the blue are both excellent choices.

Industry observers note that good doesn’t always mean expensive. A big ol’ dive watch isn’t appropriate for every occasion or every guy. Simpler can be better. Like this under-$100 life-proof G-Shock. It treads the line between classic G-Shock aesthetics and little Casio reference. A watch equally appropriate for a man who never thinks about watches or one who is always thinking about watches—Schrödinger’s timepiece of no taste or good taste. And, hot take, it pairs better with a suit than sneakers do. Keep your shoes formal and let your watch carry the high-low combo.

If he’s not a G-Shock man, he may be an Ironman. A Timex Ironman, that is, even if he’s not logging an insane amount of weekend mileage. As the world grows wary of increased technocracy-driven smart designs, there’s a simple nostalgia to the ’90s-tech runner’s watch. Turns out they were right all along. You don’t need a phone on your wrist, just a stopwatch and an alarm clock and a 100-lap memory to boot. I also like the orange accents here. If he is midwestern frugal and would object to a gift over $100, this scaled-back version also plays.

Shinola’s Duck Watch references ’60s and ’70s skin divers, which sounds dirty but really is just a term for smaller, less depth-rated dive watches and the culture of free diving and spearfishing around them. That’s a reductive explanation that some watch nerds will quibble with, but it’ll serve us for now. The two notable things to take away are 1) there was a magazine of the same name that you can find on eBay and 2) Shinola’s modern version is a killer watch. I have this one in Canary Yellow, but I recently borrowed the upcoming Mallard Brown colorway for a photo shoot, and I love it. Hated to send it back. In the sun, the dial turns almost iridescent, like the titular duck’s feathers. It’s battery powered, water-resistant, and not fussy at all.

[Editor’s note: The Mallard Brown colorway is presently out of stock, so for the time being we will direct you to the Canary.].

Let’s get fancy. But let’s get fancy with purpose. More on Rolexes soon, but I think Panerai makes the most exciting watches in the $5,000 to $15,000 range. I realize that’s a large range, one encompassing the price of a decent motorcycle or a used Camry, but I’m talking luxury Swiss-made watches here. This is the tip of the iceberg. Panerai has design panache and exquisite movements, a design that’s not too “look at me” but still far enough outside the classic mold that it demands a second look. It’s not a watch for everyone, but man, those who will love it will love it immensely.

In a recent development, recently I hosted a friend and fellow style writer for a will-not-be-named rival publication at the Detroit headquarters of T-shirt maker Soft Goods MFG. He had a couple enviable pieces (understated Nitty Gritty corduroy jacket, Paraboot derbies, perfectly faded vintage Levi’s), but I kept looking at his watch, a Unimatic Quattro. In the interest of individuality and my own love of a good suede, I’m suggesting this Todd Snyder collab as the next gift for that extra-special man in your life. It’s Unimatic with a twist, Italian design with an Americana POV, like spaghetti western for your wrist. Clint Eastwood fans rejoice.

Timex and J. Crew’s recent trout-forward collab watch sold out in an instant—unfortunately before I could get my hands on one. But there are other options for the outdoorsy dude. Especially one who cares about stopping forest fires. This Vero Smokey Bear option toes the line between campy and classy with aplomb. It’ll look good while you’re chopping wood or a little Wes Anderson–y at the lodge with a glass of bourbon in hand, telling stories about the trout that got away.

TAG can get a bad rap in the watch-collecting community, but ignore the critics, especially if your intended recipient is a racing enthusiast. TAG Heuer has a long history in F1 and Grand Prix, and it looks as much at home in the cockpit of a fancy Brad Pitt–piloted car as it does in the fan stands or the sports bar. If you want to step it up a level, the Monaco is a luxury take on a race-day watch—all European angles and rich leather.

This is the only pilot’s watch on the list—and for good reason. It’s the most handsome pilot’s watch on the market. Marathon developed these in partnership with the Kelly Air Force Base in 1986 and specced it out to withstand high-altitude flight, or even an ejection. If you’re in the market for a classic pilot’s chronograph, Bremont makes the best one. But if you are in the market for a no-frills, all-style, practically designed pilot’s watch, the Marathon Arctic Navigator is your ticket.

In a recent development, maybe he’s a Rolex Pepsi guy, but you’re on a non-Swiss-made budget. I’ll let you in on a secret: Seiko makes a pretty damn good approximation. I particularly like that this one is PADI co-branded and automatic, with a 200 meter depth rating. Even better, it’s under $500.

For my money, Doxa makes some of the most interesting dive watches out there. Is this on the list because I’d really love if someone took the hint and bought one for me? Hard to say. What’s easy to say is that the orange-dial Doxa Sub 200T is a showstopper. It’s got a slightly smaller profile and a more interesting silhouette than the original 200 but still retains the necessary details, like its unidirectional rotating bezel with its integrated U.S. Navy no-decompression limit table. No rules on whether that’s used underwater or just at the dinner table, either. It’s good to know how long to cook a steak for.

Beating the cold has gotten that much easier with the rise of blanket coats. This winter, we’re staying bundled up, not only with stylish layering tricks like wraps, shawls, and capes, but by blending the two.

Blanket coats have become the cold-weather item fashion people are loving, and it was all over a lot of the fall/winter 2026 runways, too. So, it’s clear that the style is making the rounds, and there’s no need to wait for next winter to finally be tuned in. Blanket coats provide the coziness of at-home comfort, snuggled beneath a good quilt, to your everyday outfits.

It has been revealed that and most serve a two-in-one purpose, also providing some neck protection, so you can opt out of scarves sometimes, or double up if you’re dealing with some really cold days. Below, I’ve gathered some stylish ways to lean into the popular blanket coat trend this fall and winter.

If you’re looking for something that feels a bit elevated, try a blanket coat similar to this style with draping that bunches and gathers flawlessly, giving an almost regal vibe.

Industry observers note that if you’re not big on layering, let the coat do the layering for you. Leaning into a blanket jacket like this one that’s split open at the front makes it look like you’re wearing more pieces than you actually are.

Sources indicate that the blanket coat serves as a literal wrap-around sweater that keeps you cozy and stylish. This black with brown trim one is perfect for your every day.

In a recent development, while some blanket coats wrap, others fall like trenches, but carry a bit thicker material like the one above. Pairing a simple neutral-colored piece with a monotone outfit is the easy way in.

Sources indicate that the best part of a good blanket style coat is that it keeps you covered without having to deal with a zipper. If you want a more relaxed-fit coat then a style like this is great.

For those days when you wish you could carry around a massive blanket with you, try instead pulling out your thickest coat that gives all the vibes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that most people don’t think of Thanksgiving when they think of holiday movies. Halloween and Christmas? of course. Valentine’s Day? You bet! But outside of John Hughes’s 1987 comedy Planes, Trains and Automobiles starring Steve Martin and John Candy, Hollywood still struggles to really capture the feeling of Thanksgiving on film.

Industry observers note that that’s not to say that filmmakers aren’t trying. The thirty films below capture all the fall vibes, family squabbles, and strenuous meal planning that come with Thanksgiving dinner—even if some of them don’t technically take place on Thanksgiving. (Still, I tried my best to keep those at a minimum.) If you’re looking for something to watch with the whole family, start an argument, or just feel thankful that good Thanksgiving movies do exist, these are the Thanksgiving movies that are actually worth watching.

You won’t find a Thanksgiving movie list without Planes, Trains and Automobiles. The 1987 John Hughes comedy is a genuine classic—arguably so good that no one’s made a better Thanksgiving film since. How could they? The story follows a marketing executive (played by Steve Martin) who just wants to get home to Fresh York for Thanksgiving on the busiest travel day of the year. Instead, he spends the entire three-day trip across the country with a chatty shower ring salesman (John Candy). Despite Martin’s prickliness, they’re forced to bond over the holiday while sharing the kind of heartfelt laughs that most movies nowadays just can’t replicate with the same sincerity anymore.

This is one of the movies that that you’ll see on the list that is more about fall than it is about Thanksgiving, but You’ve Got Mail does include a Thanksgiving scene. In this 1998 romantic comedy starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan and written and directed by Nora and Delia Ephron, two Upper West Side Latest Yorkers meet in an online chat room and fall in love over a series of months. At one point, Tom Hanks walks into Zabar's on Thanksgiving, which is maybe the most New York thing one can do.

It has been revealed that jodie Foster's finest directorial effort remains this 1995 comedy about the Thanksgiving get-together of Holly Hunter's thoroughly dysfunctional clan, which includes her mother (Anne Bancroft) and father (Charles Durning), her brother (Robert Downey Jr.), and his friend (Dylan McDermott). What ensues is the gold standard for family-gathering holiday films, full of absurdity, pathos, and ultimately a rousing sense of the ups and downs of dealing with relatives.

Industry observers note that an ensemble cast of Vanessa Williams, Vivica A. Fox, Nia Long, and Michael Beach star in this comedy-drama film about a Black American family that gets together every Sunday to have dinner. But when Significant Mama (Irma P. Hall) falls ill, her three daughters’ strained relationships take on an entirely new form. While the meals never occur on Thanksgiving Day, the family arguments over a mouth-watering meal do.

Remember the Titans isn't technically a Thanksgiving movie either. But it features plenty of those Thanksgiving elements—football, fall foliage, and large amounts of people gathering for meals. The film stars Denzel Washington as a high school football coach who is brought in to teach at a predominately white school in Alexandria, Virginia. And if it’s not playing on cable on Thanksgiving anyway—that is, if you haven’t cut the cord yet—I’m sure a streaming service picked it up for the holiday.

Maybe it's not as iconic as A Charlie Brown Christmas or It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, but this Peanuts holiday special is a good holdover between Halloween and Christmas. This Emmy-winning classic sees Peppermint Patty infiltrating Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving holiday, which he naturally scrambles to put together with his trademark anxiety. (Where the hell are these kids' parents, by the way?).

Spike Lee's iconic She's Gotta Have It, following one woman's love square with her three competing lovers, isn't typically included in the wholesome holiday canon. But few films have featured a more memorable Thanksgiving dinner than that of Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns), in which she invites over all three men to celebrate the holiday together as she sits at the head of the table.

In a recent development, opening and closing with scenes of its characters at Thanksgiving dinner, Woody Allen's 1986 comedic drama—which won him an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay and Best Supporting Actor and Actress statuettes for Michael Caine and Dianne Wiest, respectively—tells a raft of interconnected stories, all in some way related to Mia Farrow's Hannah and her two siblings. Equal parts hilarious and touching, it remains one of the writer-director's crowning achievements.

It’s not the holidays if you haven’t watched a Lifetime movie with the family yet. Still, that doesn’t mean you must subject yourself to the most baseless shlock. How about a simple, magic family film from the creator of the Muppets. Well, posthumously, that is. And yes, that means puppets—but that should only be a plus!

It has been revealed that knives Out just screams cozy with all of its sweaters, wooden decorations, and fallen leaves. Rian Johnson's mystery flick, which is now a trilogy, is a must-watch if you're in a family that loves solving puzzles or escape rooms (or, you know, Daniel Craig). Hopefully, your Thanksgiving isn’t anywhere near as chaotic.

Industry observers note that okay, so, technically this would be more faithful to the Thanksgiving canon if it were Turkey Run. But this feature-film debut from the iconic Aardman animation studio is a Thanksgiving hit for obvious reasons. The stop-motion film, centered on a group of chickens determined to escape execution before being turned into chicken pies, is as hilarious as it is visually spectacular.

Christmas Vacation is in a category of its own, but the entire National Lampoon franchise is usually a crowd-pleaser at family holidays. This one features Malcolm in the Middle–era Bryan Cranston as the eccentric hippie and long-lost cousin of suburban man Mitch Snider. Awkward family antics ensue.

Recent findings suggest that for the Christopher Guest and Eugene Levy fans, this 2006 mockumentary is about three actors played by Guest favorites Catherine O’Hara, Parker Posey, and Harry Shearer, who are making a film called Home for Purim, which is supposedly garnering lots of Oscar buzz. Things come to a bit of a halt when the studio intervenes and renames the film Home for Thanksgiving, changing the entire plot of the film just to chase awards.

This movie jumps around to four different Thanksgiving meals, all thrown by families from diverse backgrounds who have a few things in common: stress, food, and stressing over food. What’s Cooking? also features an ensemble cast composed of Kyra Sedgwick, Joan Chen, Lainie Kazan, Mercedes Ruehl, Maury Chaykin, Julianna Margulies, Alfre Woodard, and Dennis Haysbert.

For a little switch-up, this one is a documentary. Directed by Martin Scorsese, this film follows The Band’s Thanksgiving farewell show, featuring Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, and Eric Clapton. Alongside Stop Making Sense, The Last Waltz is often cited as one of the greatest music concert films ever made.

In a recent development, many films in the ‘40s concerned the difficulties soldiers faced when coming home from the war, but few attempted to bring our heroes home over Thanksgiving. The Very Thought of You, which is more of a romantic drama, stars Dennis Morgan and Dane Clark as they return just for the holiday—before they’re shipped back once the weekend ends. Fair warning: This one’s a bit of a tear-jerker. “You know those advertisements that show pictures of guys in uniform coming back to what they left?,” one character states in the film. “They don’t show what home really means.”.

Sources indicate that thanksgiving is anything but jovial in Ang Lee's The Ice Storm, which is set around the holiday in 1973 Connecticut, where two well-off families struggle with all manner of the-times-they-are-a'-changin' upheaval. Adultery and alcohol inevitably play a significant factor in their problems, which are dramatized by director Lee—and handled by his cast, including Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver, Tobey Maguire, Christina Ricci, and Elijah Wood—with chilling incisiveness.

In her finest performance, Katie Holmes plays the titular April, who bravely invites her dysfunctional family from suburban Pennsylvania to her tiny apartment on the Lower East Side. Disaster strikes early when her stove breaks and she is forced to find a working oven in her building. Meanwhile, her cancer-stricken mother (Oscar nominee Patricia Clarkson) slowly dreads the trek into the city to see her somewhat estranged daughter.

Industry observers note that on Thanksgiving 1983, Marty (Josh Hamilton) brings his fiancée Lesly (Parker Posey) home to meet his family—his dim-witted and horny brother, Anthony; his cold and nosey mother, Mrs. Pascal; and his mentally unhinged and Kennedy-obsessed sister, Jackie-O. All hell breaks loose, naturally, as kitchen knives are hidden, sexual boundaries are tested, and Parker Posey delivers one of the most hilariously intense performances of her career.

It has been revealed that judd Apatow's dramatic comedy stars Adam Sandler as George Simmons, a wealthy movie star who seeks to get back to his stand-up-comedy roots after being diagnosed with leukemia. He meets a young aspiring comic (Seth Rogen) in search of a mentor, and the two tour the country as George performs his new material and reconnects with his ex-fiancée. It's a film about the comedy world and how friendships evolve into familial relationships, highlighted by a Thanksgiving toast George delivers in honor of his chosen family.

Trey Edward Shults made his directorial debut with this indie drama, which stars members of his real-life family—including his aunt Krisha Fairchild in the titular role. Krisha arrives at her sister's house for a Thanksgiving celebration after years of estrangement from her family. Overwhelmed by her return to this seemingly normal life, Krisha starts drinking and popping pills in secret—and all hell breaks loose as emotions fly and family secrets are exposed.

Much like Krisha above, The Humans is for people who really can’t stand Thanksgiving. Based on Stephen Karam’s Tony Award-winning play, the film stars a family played by Richard Jenkins, Jayne Houdyshell, Amy Schumer, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and June Squibb as they all just tear into each other over Thanksgiving dinner.

Recent findings suggest that this sequel to the big-screen adaptation of the classic TV sitcom finds the spooky-ooky Addams family once again up to their weird, gothic ways. But their family is thrown into turmoil when a newly introduced nanny, Debbie (a pitch-perfect Joan Cusack), has her sights on Uncle Fester—and looks on marrying him for his riches before killing him off. Wednesday and Pugsley know something's up, but Debbie convinces Gomez and Morticia to send them to summer camp—where they are forced to participate in a completely bonkers musical rendition of the first Thanksgiving.

Folk rocker Arlo Guthrie (son of Woody) plays himself in this offbeat comedy film inspired by his song of the same name. Guthrie, a long-haired draft dodger visiting some friends in an uptight Massachusetts town for Thanksgiving, thinks he's doing his hosts a favor by filling his Volkswagen minibus with their garbage and taking it to the dump. A mix-up ensues, Guthrie is busted for littering, and he seeks to prove himself unfit for combat when the draft comes calling.

Recent findings suggest that nobody's Fool is one of the last great headlining vehicles for Paul Newman, who stars here as an upstate Upcoming York construction-worker hustler in constant conflict with a contractor (Bruce Willis) whose wife (Melanie Griffith) he fancies. His routine is upended by the arrival of his estranged son (Dylan Walsh) around Thanksgiving, leading to an amusing (and disarming) holiday-set character study about loneliness, reconciliation, and the unexpected ways people achieve contentment.

It has been revealed that over the course of a Thanksgiving weekend, Chris O'Donnell's prep-school student comes of age while caring for a blind retired Army lieutenant (Al Pacino) in Martin Brest's acclaimed Scent of a Woman, which finally earned Pacino his first-ever Academy Award (for Best Actor). Amid all of its star's blustery hoo-ahing, it's a surprisingly tender tale of an unlikely friendship between two strangers.

Jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau are two bitter lifelong rivals who engage in ludicrous warfare over the affections of the latest resident (Ann-Margret) of their Wabasha, Minnesota, neighborhood. That conflict includes an amusing Thanksgiving dinner, in which the two do their best to act like feuding, immature children.

Sources indicate that another cozy classic. Wes Anderson’s stop-motion film about a family of foxes with a killer voice cast—George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Wilem Dafoe, Owen Wilson, Brian Cox, and Adrien Brody—couldn’t be a better film to watch with your family this holiday.

Industry observers note that there’s never been a Thanksgiving-based superhero that I can recall—nor should there be—but the original Spider-Man film with Tobey Maguire features a particularly memorable Thanksgiving scene. Peter’s Aunt May invites the Osbornes over for Thanksgiving when Norman (Willem Dafoe) notices one of Peter’s injuries and deduces that he’s Spider-Man.

Eli Roth turned an actual joke project into a feature film in 2023 when he released Thanksgiving, a Halloween-esque slasher horror film about a killer let loose on Turkey Day. He wears a John Carver mask, carries an axe, and absolutely hates Black Friday. On the latter, we can all agree.

The Best Boots to Wear With Barrel Jeans This Season

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor.
  • Industry observers note that whether or not you’ve jumped on board, barrel jeans remain a favorite silhouette among the fashion set.
  • In a recent development, our conclusion: ankle boots are the best match for this sculptural cut, because they tuck neatly beneath the curved hem.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Industry observers note that whether or not you’ve jumped on board, barrel jeans remain a favorite silhouette among the fashion set. They’re quirky, fashion-forward, and, yes, undeniably comfortable, qualities that explain their staying power. I’ve been devoted to them since I got my first pair in 2022, and they’ve been my main go-to jean ever since. Now that boot season is here, we set out to find the best styles to wear with them.

In a recent development, our conclusion: ankle boots are the best match for this sculptural cut, because they tuck neatly beneath the curved hem. That said, not all ankle boots are created equal. A sleek Chelsea boot keeps the proportions clean, while a pointed-toe style adds a bit of length to balance the leg’s volume. If you lean casual, a lug-sole pair gives the look an easy, utilitarian edge. Whatever you choose, aim for a hem that skims the top of the boot, so the curve of the denim stays the star of the outfit.

Below, we’ve rounded up our favorite pairs to shop now.

Dressed up in a leopard print, this versatile kitten heel gives barrel jeans a touch of polish and plenty of personality.

City life calls for a boot that keeps up. These lace-ups bring the utility, while barrel jeans and a cozy knit bring the style.

Inspired by western silhouettes, this suede boot hugs the ankle while bringing a touch of rugged charm to everyday style.

Styled with your favorite barrel jeans, these block-heel boots give off a retro feel that’s equally cool and polished.

Classic black, a softly rounded toe, and a stable block heel. This ankle boot echoes the curve of a barrel hem and keeps the whole look beautifully balanced.

It has been revealed that warm tan suede, a sharp pointed toe, and a supportive wedge heel. Tucked beneath a barrel jean, this ankle boot adds height without sacrificing comfort.

With its pointed toe and low kitten heel, this sleek ankle boot is the finishing touch that keeps a barrel-leg look elegantly in proportion.

Chocolate croc-embossed leather, a pointed square toe, and a clean block heel make this ankle boot a polished partner for barrel jeans, textured, grounded, and quietly luxe.

Industry observers note that A cranberry red boot delivers seasonal warmth to this contemporary jean silhouette. The rounded square toe lends a modern edge while echoing the gentle shape of the barrel leg.

There’s something captivating about Chelsea boots in luminous black leather. This pair lends polish to the laid-back persona of barrel denim. With a sturdy sole and easy pull-on design, they’re as functional as they are refined.

What to Watch After Finishing MobLand

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (806 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that mobLand season 2 has come to an end.
  • Sources indicate that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series.
  • When an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that mobLand season 2 has come to an end. (For now, at least—Tom Hardy and his motley crew have already started working on the third season.) Fortunately, there's an excellent selection of reveals on Netflix that'll fill that gory Guy Ritchie–crime thriller–shaped void in your weekend watchlist. Here's our pick of the five best ones that you should stream now that season 2 is over. And if you haven’t yet, make sure to read our breakdown of MobLand’s explosive season 2 finale—and that cliffhanger.

Sources indicate that the obvious choice, if you haven't seen it already, is the other Guy Ritchie series. The Gentlemen similarly revolves around a large mob family, has a lot of gore, and has the very same wicked sense of humor.

When an aristocratic army officer returns home after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate instead of his older brother, he quickly discovers that it's at the heart of a notorious drug empire. While he initially tries to shrug it off, he quickly becomes more involved in the criminal underworld than he imagined he would ... and it seems it comes more naturally to him than he'd have hoped.

The Gentlemen is twisty, wildly entertaining, and will be the closest you'll get to something that feels like MobLand, even though the demonstrates are narratively quite different.

Recent findings suggest that dept. Q is another Netflix original that packs a punch – adapted from the Department Q novel series, it's a crazy crime thriller that only has one season so far, so is easy to catch up on (though a second is on the way).

After a top-rated detective returns to work from an attack that left his partner paralyzed and another policeman dead, he finds himself caught up in the investigation into a cold case that completely takes hold of him.

It has been revealed that the plot, the sharp sarcastic writing and the way the whole show looks are enough to make Dept. Q an excellent watch, but it's the cast (led by an outstandingly complex performance from Matthew Goode) that makes this one particularly special.

The spy thriller with the sharpest sense of humor, the most enthralling fight scenes—and, somehow amidst all the explosions—a whole lot of heart. It can be none other than Black Doves, Netflix's original espionage series that has swiftly become one of the streamer's best-loved reveals.

Helen Webb, a spy working for an organization called the Black Doves in an undercover marriage to a politician, has her position compromised, and mostly simple”'spy wife life” upended, when her lover is assassinated. In order to protect her and the secrecy of the Black Doves, her supervisor calls in an old friend to save her and sort out the mystery. However, the web of deceit proves unexpectedly complex and the three are soon in over their heads.

It has been revealed that other than being excellently acted (thanks to the legendary Keira Knightley, Ben Whishaw, Sarah Lancashire, and the supporting cast) and delightfully explosive, Black Doves is also surprisingly heartfelt, and you just can't help but root for its kooky cast. Even if they are all a bit nuts.

According to recent reports, once you're on board the Harlan Coben train, it's hard to hop off. I Will Find You, led by Sam Worthington and Severance's Britt Lower, is certainly one of the better adaptations of a Coben novel. Ridiculous, for sure, but undeniably entertaining the second you suspend your disbelief.

Five years after a man is wrongly imprisoned for the murder of his son, he receives information from his ex-wife's sister that his son might still be alive.

It has been revealed that if you've read the book (or seen enough Coben shows that you know what's coming), then maybe you won't be quite as surprised by the twists and turns in this one. That being said, it's breezy, easy-watching, and it's intensely bingeable if you're into that kind of thriller.

Aside from the sense of humor, the thing we all love most about Guy Ritchie's films and others in that realm is the stylised action sequences. If that's what you'll be missing when MobLand is over, then give Gangs of London a watch.

Based on the video game of the same name (but fortunately much better), the series revolves around the power struggles of rival gangs across London, all of which have different allegiances and international connections. When one young undercover police officer is tasked with infiltrating one of them to exploit a moment of weakness, things get ... very messy. Very fast.

It's perhaps not as funny (read: not at all comedic) as some of the other entries on this list, but it's classically gritty, gory British crime drama at its finest, and a must-see for fans of the genre.

Festive Thanksgiving Nail Ideas for Every Kind of Holiday Plan

  • They’ll be passing the cranberry sauce, raising a glass for the toast, clutching a mug of cider—you name it.
  • And this season’s nail trends are as varied as the dishes on your table, from minimalist milky neutrals for the understated host to hand-painted leaves and shimmering gold flecks for the one who loves a little drama.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that whether you’re curling up by the fire, hosting the family dinner, or bringing dessert to a Friendsgiving, a compliment-worthy manicure is a small comfort when the day gets chaotic. No matter what comes your way, at least your nails are done. And with all the passing, pouring, and photo-posing ahead, your hands are sure to get plenty of attention.

They’ll be passing the cranberry sauce, raising a glass for the toast, clutching a mug of cider—you name it. The good news is that fall offers one of the richest color palettes of the year. Think deep cranberry, burnished copper, mossy olive, and warm cinnamon, all shades that glow against autumn light and flatter nearly every skin tone.

And this season’s nail trends are as varied as the dishes on your table, from minimalist milky neutrals for the understated host to hand-painted leaves and shimmering gold flecks for the one who loves a little drama.

Ahead, check out some Thanksgiving nail ideas to inspire your next set.

You simply cannot go wrong with brown cat-eye nails. Whether you love a long almond silhouette or prefer a shorter, softer shape, this design feels rich, polished, and effortlessly autumnal.

Plaid nails in autumnal shades bring a fresh, playful spin to a fall manicure.

We love an ombré nail set, and this milky-to-espresso gradient fits right in with the season’s warm neutrals. The soft fade from creamy white to deep, coffee-bean brown feels cozy and sophisticated, like a latte in manicure form.

This butternut-squash yellow adds a fun pop of color to a darker fall palette.

Industry observers note that coffee-glazed nails are the manicure equivalent of a warm mug in your hands. It’s an easy pick for anyone who wants a little shimmer without going full metallic.

Can’t pick one fall shade? Wear them all, one on each finger. You’ll be surprised how well they work together.

Rich cherry red nails get a glam upgrade with a delicate gold cuticle line, a classic shade with a jewelry-box finish.

Deep, velvety, and effortlessly chic, this forest-inspired hue pairs beautifully with gold jewelry and cozy knits.

Brown nails with a white chrome topcoat melt into a frosty, taupe-y shade that’s simply stunning.

Rich, moody, and perfectly autumnal, this duo looks like a cranberry-and-herb tablescape on your fingertips.

Tortoiseshell nails are the chicest way to bring warm amber and espresso swirls to your Thanksgiving look.

Sheer, creamy, and effortlessly polished, this minimalist shade pairs with everything from cable-knit sweaters to your fanciest holiday dress.

Delicate, understated, and just a little whimsical, this look pairs a sheer neutral base with one or two hand-painted leaves and a dark French-tip manicure.

In a recent development, before you turn up your favorite song and hit the open road, make sure your latest baby is protected. It can be a lot to take in, so let’s demystify insurance. Here’s what you need to know.

Rate: This is the baseline estimated price that would cover the potential cost of future claims. It’s determined using shared group factors such as age group; if you’re in your twenties, it would take into account the statistical driving information for other 25-year-olds in a region.

Premium: This is the adjusted individual insurance price that you’ll pay over a six- or 12-month period. It’s created by starting with the rate, then adding more specific factors that affect your claim risk level. These include your driving record, claims history, mileage usage, and vehicle type.

In a recent development, overwhelmed? Don’t sweat it—State Farm can get you an insurance quote before you buy.

To answer that when it comes to car ownership, consider how much you drive annually (to avoid leasing mileage overages if you exceed the stated mileage), how long you initiative to keep your vehicle, and your financial situation.

Industry observers note that then, know that there are insurance differences between leasing and buying, too. Leasing companies adhere to stricter requirements than those that most states set, which could translate into higher monthly premiums.

If you buy to avoid the mileage caps and wear-and-tear of leasing, but still want the benefits of a fresh ride every few years, there is a moment during your payment strategy when you can get a newly introduced car. Your initial loan payments largely go to interest (what lenders charge for giving you money), but there’s a break-even point when your payments begin going to principal (the actual amount you’ve borrowed). When that happens, and the outstanding balance is equal to the value of the car, you can trade it in for that amount, which is a budget-friendly way to upgrade.

Whatever you choose, a little strategy will keep you in the driver’s seat from dreaming about your new car to signing on the dotted line.

According to recent reports, no further questions: All’s Fair season 2 is one of the most fashionable series you can stream right now. When the show debuted just over a year ago, it made headlines for being Hulu’s biggest scripted launch in three years. Is it any wonder? It combines drama, style, and female powerhouses with major personality.

Recent findings suggest that the show follows stylish lawyers played by Kim Kardashian, Naomi Watts, Sarah Paulson, Niecy Nash-Betts, Teyana Taylor, and Glenn Close, each with their own distinct aesthetics that range from extremely rare archival ’90s vintage to quiet luxury glam. All’s Fair season 2 debuted a few weeks ago and is well underway, with the finale airing on Wednesday, Dec. 2, 2026. While we wait for the next episodes, we caught up with Paula Bradley, the costume designer behind it all.

It has been revealed that when we started out with the new season, we did have a note from Ryan Murphy just to tone it down a little, not a lot, but just a little, in regard to that they are lawyers, not to do so many hats on Niecy—it’s hard for the eyeline. Then it was really just about combing through the season’s collections and seeing who did what, and which silhouettes go where, because at this point we’ve kind of developed our characters. The substantial difference for season 2 was we really upped our jewelry game.

So, it started with Glenn. She had asked if she could have some real pearls that she just wore all the time. And so we wrote to Tiffany’s, and then we wrote to everybody, we found jewelers that we’d never heard of that did fantastical things. Tiffany loaned us three incredible brooches that were so ridiculously valuable, and some pearls and diamonds and earrings for Glenn. Boucheron did jewelry for everybody for the Scorpio Ball. We had to have fresh safes installed in the office and in the truck.

Yes. We bought a lot of vintage for Teyana Taylor. We had vintage Alaïa and Gaultier, and we bought an incredible vintage outfit that—I can’t say who wears it in the end—we bought this Galliano runway piece that I had them split into two invoices so that I could put it in the budget. There was a sweater set that was really, really stunning. I don’t dress Kim, Soki Mak dresses Kim. She starts with just going to the auction houses and the vintage places around Europe and Paris, and just collecting everything that she can for Kim.

So, if we start with Sarah Paulson, who plays Carr, she’s the most edgy of all of the characters. She always has a shoulder, sometimes it’s the softer shoulder, but mostly it’s a very sharp shoulder. It was based on the old Saint Laurent. She always has a feminine moment, so the bows have become her—significant bows, big earrings, and moments of softness just to soften it up.

Then Naomi Watts (Liberty Ronson) is our quiet luxury. She walks into everything, and she’s monochromatic, although this season we started to pull her a little bit more into the dark side.

Niecy Nash-Betts (Emerald)—it was hard to lose the hats for Niecy, so we went into the belts because her waist is so snatched. And Niecy, for me, represents her own culture incredibly well. That body is so Jessica Rabbit, and it’s so for real. And so she’s always about color, sass, attitude, and glamour. I would say she’s the most glamorous of my characters.

Glenn Close (Dina) is our classic. She’s our classic WASP. So her clothes usually have embroidery or a little bit of extra texture, or she always has a lace edge. She’s a little bit more heirloom, you know? Old Hollywood.

Sources indicate that I can. So, I can’t give away the ending because it hasn’t landed yet, and it’s quite a shocker. But obviously the opening, and re-creating the scorpion cape (for Kim) was amazing, because there still are a few ladies who do that beading, who did it in the ’50s and ’60s for Judy Garland and Liza Minnelli, and worked with Bob Mackie. They dip those beads into different solutions of bleach to age them appropriately. They pulled threads to get the edges a little bit frayed. And I worry that that talent and that skill set will soon have disappeared. So that was amazing.

According to recent reports, the other thing that I love is the Balenciaga bright yellow highlighter coat that Sarah wears, because she always wears black or gray. And that moment of her just walking through the hallways in that giant oversize cocoon coat, and the glasses and the shoes—we did it just like the runway—was a real joy.

And Naomi, we got her in a couple of Saint Laurent pieces with stronger shoulders, and that was great, too. But the opening—that was supposed to be the opening, but it’s actually the second scene—is also my favorite. So we made Sarah a leather shirt with a giant leather bow, with the shoulders, and Glenn had been at the Erdem show in London, and so we put Glenn in that fabulous denim suit with all the white embroidery. I think it just set the season off.

Industry observers note that sarah has the Fendi that came off the runway this season. And Sarah’s really the only one with a bag game, because she comes in and out of the law firm. So she still carried the Prada from last season into this season, but she also has a really great Balenciaga bag.

I think it’s more the totes—when they have them, it’s the tote bags, because that’s their professional, legal side. They all have a set of work totes that you believe that they could pull documents out of. I think that’s probably the most relatable. I think we all, even though it’s not good for our shoulders, it’s not good for our backs, most women I know, we all have a set of really great tote bags that we put our very heavy computers in and carry all our stuff in. We like a good tote, and I think that’s probably the most relatable part of it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was chosen by an ELLE editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

Welcome to In Good Organization, where we ring in the festive season with fashion-insider entertaining tips, expert etiquette advice, and the perfect editor-approved hostess gifts.

In a recent development, holiday entertaining brings with it countless conundrums—from uninvited guests to the cousin who won’t put down their phone—for both hosts and guests. Agility is the key word; being able to elegantly pivot and respond to unexpected situations is what makes people feel comfortable and appreciated. Just in time for festive gatherings, ELLE spoke with Lizzie Post, author, co-president of the Emily Post Institute, and co-host of the Awesome Etiquette podcast, about all the things to keep in mind for a kind and gracious holiday. Read on for Post’s refreshingly down-to-earth tips.

No one can keep up with the incredible party décor shown on influencers’ posts, and you don’t have to try. Elegance can be found in any space, so host within the realities of your home. “You are not meant to be entertaining at the level of someone with a million-dollar budget and a gigantic home. You get to entertain at exactly your level, whatever that is,” Post says. “All the little touches and the things you do to make people feel comfortable and welcome in your home are what make for a great host.”.

Bringing the wrong item can be an error on the part of the guest, but hosts should always make sure to minimize discomfort. “You want to take the etiquette high road and let it not be a problem. If [someone brings] an extra guest, quickly enlist someone from your household or a trusted guest to help you zhuzh the arrangements in a discreet way so that the extra person does not feel like they were not meant to be there… [We have] the nearest-and-dearest to the host take smaller portions, so that everyone can have a decent portion.”.

It has been revealed that part of smartphone etiquette is letting others make their own choices. “You don’t overly control someone’s phone usage. Their rudeness will show on its own and will be noticed by more than just you… [Saying] ‘Could you make sure your phone is off, so you’re not tempted to use it throughout the evening?’ That is not a polite thing, even though it sounds gentle and so reasonable. That’s micromanagement.”.

Bringing a thoughtful gift is always appreciated, but truly engaging with the event is what really matters. “There is no burden for hosting you. You’ve been invited and should feel welcome and like you belong in this space. You are not there to repay the efforts of the host. We are greeting our host. We are engaging with the other people. We are helping ourselves to the refreshments that are offered. If there are games or entertainment, we’re participating in that. If there’s a theme, we’ve revealed up in the theme. That’s really how we’re a good guest.”.

Industry observers note that always say goodbye. “At the end of the night, say thank you and goodbye and seek out the host, whether it’s a substantial open house party or it’s a small dinner party to make that connection and express gratitude before we go.”.

Serving an item that a guest brought is at the host’s discretion. “A hostess gift is a hostess gift. It is not meant to be used that night with the people who brought it. It can be, but it does not have to be.”.

Sources indicate that whether you mail a card or not, make sure to share your appreciation with your host. “Thank-you notes are a wonderful idea and they allow you an extra level of expression, a little more thought. It doesn’t mean that a text message the next day would not also be appreciated. Any version of thanking your host after a party is a great version.”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

15 Best Beard Oils for Taming Your Stubborn Facial Hair

📅 08 Dec 2016 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3630 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love.
  • I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most important beard care product, just after beard trimmers.
  • Sources indicate that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So, you've realized. Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love. Thankfully, the best beard oil will keep that sculpted scruff feeling great! And not just for you, either, because the right beard oil leaves your skin glowing—and stops your facial hair from annoying any partner who gets close to it. Great beard oils also keep coarse hair from getting brittle and wiry, and soften your beard so you’re not scratching your neck or dealing with beard dandruff (yes, it exists). All that from just a couple drops of wonder oil.

I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most important beard care product, just after beard trimmers. And it’s a close second. Because whether you keep your facial hair at a precise 24-hour stubble, go full hermit-mode, or stay somewhere in between, a beard oil does irreplaceable work. (The kind you can’t replace with any old moisturizer or conditioner.) So, if you’re tired of flyaways, coarse beard hair, dandruff, or itchiness, these GQ-tested and approved beard oils will turn your scruff into fluff. Promise.

Sources indicate that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer. (At the time of writing, we’re talking nearly 30,000 reviews and a 4.5-star rating.) And often, I'll intentionally seek out an alternative to these Amazon-beloved grooming products—if only because it feels like the equivalent of recommending Applebee's to an out-of-towner. But this time, well: Welcome to Applebee's.

Industry observers note that frankly, I couldn't find a better beard oil. Not only is Honest Amish cost-effective (at the second-best price-per-ounce on my list), but the brand nailed the blend. It's a pure oil recipe (no non-oil ingredients), with seven carrier oils and seven essential oils that give it an earthy scent and help tone the skin beneath your bushel. It absorbs fast, works great to smooth down flyaways, relax stiff bristles, and battle both dry skin and flake-prone beards. And did I mention the value? Six bucks per ounce is a steal.

Industry observers note that to be clear, I only use Honest Amish on my beard, largely because I'm not a fan of using any essential oils on bare skin—I particularly find that pumpkin seed oil (a key ingredient here) can be slightly pore-clogging on acne-prone skin. That mentioned: I count myself as acne-prone and haven't had challenges with Honest Amish, so I'm probably being over-cautious. It's really just that good.

It has been revealed that despite the name Beardbrand, this company's product line covers the whole body, with a focus on multi-tasking grooming products like dual washes, all-purpose balms, and this utilitarian oil. You'll catch me using it on my hands, elbows, and hair—whether for a dash of shine (to offset a matte hair product) or a protective coat against frizz and humidity. But Beardbrand's Utility Oil is on this list because it works beautifully in the beard.

It has been revealed that sure, it's a touch heavier than some other oils—but that also makes it a terrific pre-shave lubricant. It's important to note that no matter which “flavor” you choose, this oil has a strong dash of fragrance. They're all good, but I'm partial to the brand's newly introduced Bold Fortune scent, which oozes a sexy combo of leather, oud, and tobacco. (And pro-tip: The brand's utility wash has the same come-hither scent, if you want to double down.).

In a recent development, horace's beard oil will make a lot of you happy, though for different reasons. For those overwhelmed by scents—particularly artificial ones—you'll appreciate that its got the subtlest of aromas. I'm partial to the Lemon & Mint one, which reads as “fresh" and never overwhelms. For those looking to stay away from chemicals, Horace's formula is 99% natural—and the 1% is a synthetic grapeseed oil, not something with 12 syllables, which I'm fine with.

Sources indicate that the brand gets bonus marks for its easily-understood ingredients labels, which break down these details and err on the side of much-appreciated transparency. Finally, if you're on the fence about beard oils, Horace will make you a believer. It absorbs fast, gives a pinch of shine, and makes just enough difference in terms of taming, moisturizing, and softening that you'll see why a beard oil makes sense.

In the grooming world, Jack Black (the brand) has earned its own fanbase, thanks in large part to one product—the signature Jack Black beard oil. Apply just a few drops and it immediately goes to work softening coarse and brittle facial hair, and without an overpowering fragrance that will distract you all day long. It's one of the most popular beard oils on Amazon, but don't hold that against it. While it softens and adds shine, this oil also delivers a dose of antioxidants and vitamins from natural ingredients such as brown algae and rosemary.

It also uses a unique blend of oils with the subtlest whiff of melon fragrance. Instead of the usual suspects (jojoba, avocado, sunflower seed), this product uses Kalahari melon oil, marula oil, and plum oil, which moisturize your facial hair and skin on contact. Because these oils are all fast-absorbing (my beard hair soaks it up like a sponge), they make this product much less greasy than other beard oils, giving it a more premium feel.

I test literally hundreds of grooming products a year, and I'm so intimately acquainted with brands new and old that I often think about them based on their best product. For Pura d'Or, it's this organic beard oil. It's the best value on this list, at $3 per fluid ounce. Given how rapidly you can go through beard oil—just think, if you're applying up to twice a day, that dollar-per-ounce math becomes crucial. So, in addition to being my budget pick, this also gets my recommendation as the best beard oil for big beards.

Of course, it's only notable if the formula measures up—and here, it does. There are two carrier oils, argan and jojoba, along with a bit of grapefruit peel and some sandalwood essential oil for both a natural scent and a touch of antimicrobial powers. It's a great beard oil for anyone, no matter how significant your bank account, but if you're bearding on a budget, you'll appreciate how much goodness Pura d'Or packs into a few bucks.

Sources indicate that blind Barber's tonka-tinged oil is wonderful for the guy who wants to moisturize skin and whiskers with the same product. It wears extremely light—so much so that my oily skin barely registers its presence—and I find its carrier-oil-centric and shea-butter-forward formula especially comforting on the skin. It should be noted that this formula includes artificial perfume, so fragrance-averse individuals should steer clear. But for those of us who want a special scent, a flake-free beard, and soothed skin, Blind Barber's beard oil does it all.

In a recent development, while I'd use most of the above options as both a hair oil and a beard oil, Aesop's is one where I think of it as a hair oil first and foremost. It brings control without making things look greasy, while trapping moisture and stopping frizz. I'll use it in short hair to tame down the sides, in medium lengths (mixed with a cream or clay) for added shine, or in long hair to prevent split ends. Then, once my hair's settled up, I'll run my hands through my beard afterward. So, if you want a great hair oil with beard benefits, Aesop's is the winner.

Recent findings suggest that since the beginning of the men's grooming boom, I've been waiting for the substantial designer fashion houses to start catering to guys with facial hair. For now, Tom Ford's beard oil stands alone. So, how does the designer oil stack up against our everyday favorites? After trying it out, I can tell you it’s better as a fragrance than a beard oil, but the scent alone earns it a spot in this guide.

In a recent development, the tobacco vanilla fragrance is much more sophisticated than what we’re used to seeing, or smelling, in this space. The scent puts an emphasis on vanilla, and you just need one or two pumps for full coverage. Considering the price and the name on the bottle, we were shocked to find this oil comes in a plastic pump bottle, but that fragrance. If you want to buy beard oil as a gift, this premium conditioning oil is a step up over your average Amazon brand, even if it doesn't soften coarse hair as well as some of our other options.

Sources indicate that if you have sensitive skin—or if you're afraid of your beard oil clashing with your daily cologne—then Marlowe makes one of the only fragrance-free beard oils. Most beard oil formulas contain both essential oils and some type of perfume oil (or, parfum, for my fellow ingredients detectives), which can be risky for your skin, follicles, and pores, so it’s nice to have an option for acne-prone and sensitive skin types.

Industry observers note that this beard oil couldn’t be simpler—and I mean that in a good way. Marlowe No. 143 has an all-oil formula and just four ingredients: safflower seed oil, sunflower seed oil, corn oil, and soybean oil. That’s it. Considering the average beauty product contains up to a dozen ingredients we can’t even pronounce, it’s a refreshing change. Although, I have to say, if you want the softest possible beard, Honest Amish also makes a fragrance-free oil.

According to recent reports, most guys use beard oil to tame flyaways. But what if you want the thickest, fullest beard possible? In that case, I’d recommend reaching for Bevel’s oil. This brand makes skin and hair products for Black men, but anyone with coarse or curly hair can benefit from their products. GQ contributor Timothy Beck Werth reports that this oil gave him a thicker-looking beard without excess frizz, which isn't easy to do. (BTW, that’s as much as you can expect from any beard oil, so please don’t fall for the “beard growth serums” you’ll find all over the internet.).

It has been revealed that for parched facial hair, the grapeseed, macadamia, jojoba, and argan oil will condition your beard and add a healthy shine. For beneath the scruff, the avocado and primrose oil with soothe your skin without clogging up your pores and follicles. Werth says this beard oil instantly softened his facial hair, and he also liked the sweeter smell of the macadamia-based formula. Most beard oils opt for woodsy fragrances, and the more subtle scent profile here is a nice surprise, he explains.

Anthony’s conditioning beard oil is a 2-in-1 product—a pre-shave oil and regular beard oil. That approach can be risky, since a lot of multipurpose products try to be everything and succeed at nothing, but luckily that’s not the case here. If you regularly cycle between clean-shaven, stubble, and full-on lighthouse keeper, then you can still use this product daily. As a pre-shave oil, it moisturizes the skin and softens facial hair for a smoother shave with fewer morning-after red bumps. As a beard oil, it hydrates, then locks in that moisture so your beard stays soft and shiny all day. I found the consistency to be somewhere in between a leave-in conditioner gel and a traditional oil, making it thicker and less messy to apply.

Sources indicate that the oil also has an herbaceous, minty fragrance that’s so refreshing it feels like aromatherapy every time you run it through your hair. That’s because the formula is full of ingredients that smell good, feel good, and actually help your skin and hair. It uses carrier oils like soybean and castor to deliver skin-pleasing and antimicrobial botanicals such as rosemary, basil, tea tree oil, eucalyptus, and spearmint. And on the hydration front, calendula and olive oil nourish your whiskers into their softest, fluffiest selves. Because of the more complex fragrance and ingredients profile, this wouldn’t be my pick for guys with sensitive skin. Still, it’s a multi-functional serum you’ll look forward to using every day.

Lots of beard oils promise to get flyaways under control, yet those rogue hairs keep popping up. So, what do you do? Instead of trying yet another oil, try reaching for a product that’s more of a leave-in conditioner for your beard. We’ve previously praised Zeus’s beard brushes, but the California-based brand also makes a beard serum that deserves a spot in your bathroom cabinet. I love that this beard oil has the simplest possible ingredients list: sweet almond oil, soybean oil, argan seed oil, trihydroxystearin, avocado oil, and fragrance.

The only multi-syllable ingredient there is a simple thickening agent, which gives this refined beard oil a gel-like consistency. That thicker formula will also put flyaways in their place. The very subtle fragrance is more Mediterranean than winter pine forest (we tested the Verbena Lime version), but you can also opt for a fragrance-free formula if you have sensitive skin or allergies. The plastic bottle uses an air pump, letting you get every last drop of oil. For clean freaks who hate the messiness and spillage that always comes with beard oil application, this is another bonus.

Industry observers note that tired of being left out of couple’s skincare night just because those stupid sheet masks won’t hold onto your glorious beard? Cardon’s got you, boo. Actually, this bead oil hack is perfect for guys who only sparingly use beard oil on an as-needed basis.

The bamboo and charcoal sheet mask is specially shaped for guys with beards, and each mask comes with a dose of beard oil made with argan and jojoba oil. In the Venn diagram of Korean skincare and beard care products, this sheet mask-beard oil duo is the tiny, microscopic bit of overlap in the middle.

The best best oil should support your skin and your beard, and Baxter of California's sweet-smelling oil doesn't sacrifice one for the other. In his guide to the best beard care products, GQ's Timothy Beck Werth said that “In our testing, no beard oil absorbs as promptly or spreads as evenly as this one.” Squalane helps nourish the most overlooked skin on your face, while avocado oil, vitamin E, and botanical extracts smooth out your beard.

In a recent development, as with anything you put on your skin, the ingredients are what matter most. And with beard oils, there are two categories of ingredients: carrier oils and essential oils. No two ingredients will perform exactly the same. Some will help with very specific situations or conditions; some may actively aggravate your skin. Essential oils in particular can aggravate skin if used by themselves. So, consider the following carrier oils and essential oils, favored both by myself and Alyssa Bachowski, a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg, NYC barbershop.

Sources indicate that carrier oils—often vegetable and see oils—make up the bulk of these beard oil formulas, bringing beard nourishment and skin hydration. The most popular carrier oils are argan oil and jojoba oil (both of which Bachowski recommends), though there are dozens of varieties, from castor to marula to grape seed oils. They're usually unscented, though some—like coconut oil—may carry an aroma. Because carrier oils make up the “base” of the oil, they should be among the first to appear in a product's formula or list of ingredients.

In a recent development, “Jojoba oil is non-comedogenic, which means it will not clog your pores. It is also a lighter oil that is absorbent, so it won't just sit on top of the hair and give you a greasy appearance,” Bachowski notes. Along with argan oil, you’re going to see a lot of jojoba oil in most popular beard oil blends.

“Argan oil is filled with a ton of vitamins and minerals, as well as linoleic acid, sterolins, and squalene. All of these aid in protecting and keeping your skin and beard healthy,” Bachowski says.

Recent findings suggest that “Castor oil is known for promoting beard hair growth,” notes Bachowski. It’s hypothetically the best beard-growth oil of the crew, because it acts like a vitamin for your strands—though there's more on that below in the FAQs. But don't expect it to grow more hairs, or thicker hairs. Castor oil does have a smoke-and-mirrors benefit, at least. “It is a heavier oil and dark in color, so it can give the appearance of a denser beard on men with dark facial hair,” Bachowski says.

Grape seed oil can help tone down your skin's oil production, and is extremely moisturizing for scruff and skin alike.

Rich in fatty acids, this is a frontrunner for “most nourishing oil” for your skin and whiskers.

Yes, shea butter is in fact a carrier oil, and it has supremely moisturizing properties that make it great for detangling scraggly beards and softening stiff hairs.

Essential oils are distillations from more potent sources, and they tend to be additive—and active—ingredients in a beard oil. These oils are typically extracted through steaming methods, and their range of benefits can include antimicrobial properties, oil-toning abilities, and soothing superpowers. Typically, any natural fragrance in a beard oil will come from essential oils. But pure essential oils can be extremely damaging to the skin.

In a recent development, “You should not apply pure essential oil to a beard—it will do the opposite of what you are trying to achieve,” Bachowski says. “These [pure oils] are not good for your beard nor your skin. as they can be irritating and harmful. Essential oils can cause dryness, itchiness, and redness—and some people may have allergic reactions to them.” This is exactly why you want beard oils from trusted, tested brand.

In a recent development, bachowski likes cedarwood oil for its naturally astringent properties. “It helps cleanse the pores and prevent ingrown hairs,” she adds. It also adds a natural fragrance.

“Sandalwood has anti-inflammatory properties that help reduce any skin irritation,” Bachowski notes of this deliciously scented oil.

According to recent reports, lavender helps calm inflammation and redness, claims Bachowski. Plus it brings lavender's soothing scent.

This antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, oil-toning ingredient is terrific for acne-prone faces and oily skin types.

Along with its refreshing scent, grapefruit peel oil helps nourish and detangle.

Recent findings suggest that as GQ's lead grooming product reviewer, I've tried just about every beard oil in the biz. The ones chosen for this roundup excel at protecting and moisturizing both skin and hair, with minimal risk for things like inverse reactions and blemishes. They absorb cleanly, unless they expressly choose not to (like those which expressly use silicone), and they smell terrific (with both natural and artificially scented options). I've tested beard oils for a decade, on a beard that's been long, short, and everything in between. I've also scoured online reviews to confirm that these products are backed by throngs of loyal fans, whose collective opinion echoes my own experiences.

What is the best beard oil according to GQ?

With more than a decade of testing beard oils under his belt, GQ’s expert tester chose Honest Amish as the best beard oil. And 29,000 Amazon shoppers have rated this same product 4.5 out of 5 stars.

It has been revealed that what is the difference between beard balm vs. oil?

Both beard balm and beard oil are both terrific for facial hair—but they don't do the same job. Beard balm is optimal for taming and styling facial hair, especially at medium and longer lengths. Beard oil provides less control over the shape and style, but is excellent at softening and conditioning the hairs and the skin underneath (preventing beard itch, beard dandruff, and split ends).

Industry observers note that after using a beard wash, most beard oils are applied the same way: “Start off with 2-3 drops in the palm of your hand,” notes Bachowski. “Rub it into your hands so that it is evenly distributed from fingertips to the heel of your hand. Start by rubbing the oil with your fingertips onto the skin beneath the beard hair, then eventually working the oil from root to tip of the actual beard. Make sure to also apply oil to your neck and cheeks where you may have shaved or trimmed as well. If you feel like the 2-3 drops wasn't enough based on the length or density of your beard, apply another 2-3 drops.”.

How do you prevent beard dandruff?

Preventing beard dandruff starts with changing your skincare regimen. Namely, introducing exfoliation and moisturizing products that can get past a thick nest of facial hair. For exfoliation, look for physical scrubs (even a beard brush will work). For the best moisturizing effects, be sure to apply beard oil both morning and night. The beard oil will also soften and condition the facial hair to prevent itchiness.

Does beard oil help grow a beard?

Sources indicate that no, beard oil is not meant to help beard hair growth, whether that’s to make facial hair thicker or grow faster. To be honest, we don’t know of much that can really change your scruff's density besides a beard transplant and maybe minoxidil. Beard oil is here to make your existing beard hair softer and more cooperative, while also nourishing the skin beneath the beard—skin that’s often prone to dehydration and dandruff. It’s already doing a lot.

Sources indicate that absolutely. Beard oil is a great investment for anyone with facial hair, since it can help soften and tame your scruff while simultaneously moisturizing the skin underneath. This means no more itching, no flyaways, and no beard dandruff.

Alyssa Bachowski is a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg NYC barbershop location.

In a recent development, last Thursday, and on a bipartisan basis, the Senate approved the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), an alleged effort to “reform” the federal permitting process for things like energy projects, hard-rock mining, and, yes, data centers. At the very least, the bill lived up to one part of its clumsy title; its passage through the Senate truly was bipartisan. It passed by a 62–33 vote, and liberal Democratic senator Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island was one of its strongest advocates.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also a very big apple with more than a few razor blades concealed inside. Environmentalists have been giving BAAJA the side-eye for a number of reasons. Out in Nebraska, Democratic state chair Jane Fleming Kleeb suspects the bill is connected to a sudden revival of interest in restarting our old friend, the Keystone XL pipeline, the continent-spanning death funnel meant to bring the world’s dirtiest fossil fuel from Alberta ultimately to refineries around the world.

My problem with this whole thing is that this “kind of civil war” is taking place exclusively on the Left. Conservative Republicans, and their oligarchical allies, are forcing the action before the latest Democratic majorities take over in January. They know exactly what they want out of the bill and what they don’t want in it. The president already has mentioned there won’t be any wind farms under the provisions of this bill on his watch. (The birds! The whales!) The bill now is with the House of Representatives. May I suggest a discreet dragging of the feet? It is the holiday season, after all.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

Walk, don’t run, your next nail appointment... OPI has cracked open its polish vault, and some of the best, previously retired OPI nail polish colors have officially made their comeback. In honor of its 45th anniversary, the brand has brought back about a dozen iconic shades that mani lovers have been begging to see again, plus even more shades inspired by OGs for a grand total of 24 upcoming(ish) polishes.

Meet OPI’s Most Requested Collection, which combines several previously-retired fan favorites with some fresh shades inspired by some of the brand’s most beloved colors. The collection includes everything from vampy Lincoln Park at Midnight and nostalgic pink Mod About You Pastel to Route Beer Float, a very ‘90s, shimmery mauve. This fall 2026 collection includes 24 permanent shades, meaning these colors aren’t just making a brief cameo before disappearing again—they’re back for good. Twelve of them are offered in the classic OPI Nail Lacquer formula, while the other 12 have come back in the longer-lasting Infinite Shine option.

Whether you’re excited to reunite with an old favorite, discover a cult classic you missed the first time around, or try a fresh shade inspired by some of these icons, I highly recommend giving the full collection a scroll. To get you started, here are 12 shades from this buzzy launch that I’m especially excited to try.

She’s baaaaccckkkkk! The inky purple shade originally debuted exactly 20 years ago and is the shimmery sister to one of my all-time faves, Lincoln Park After Dark. You know those polishes that look black until the light hits them? That’s exactly what you’re getting with this ultra moody, ultra iconic shade.

According to recent reports, another shade straight from the vault, this 2012 rich, deep violet with red shimmer became an instant favorite when it originally debuted. If you love burgundy nails for the colder months, consider your next manicure handled.

In a recent development, it may be fall, but not every manicure needs to be dark and moody rn. Mod About You Pastel polish brings a soft, creamy pink into the mix, making it a pretty option for anyone who prefers a sweet, minimalist manicure over the season’s deeper shades. It’s a slightly warmer-toned sister to another one of my faves, Mod About You.

Recent findings suggest that originally released in 1997, Route Beer Float is the oldest shade OPI brought back for this collection. A mauve-meets-caramel shimmery shade makes it a particularly chic option for the chocolate brown and chai latte manicures that have been everywhere this season.

Quiet luxury nail lovers, this one’s for you. Berlin There, Doin’ That is a creamy, light taupe that puts a fresh spin on OPI’s beloved Berlin There, Done That shade. It’s a little lighter and softer than the original, with a greige-like finish that makes it the perfect understated neutral.

Sources indicate that OPI Ink fans, rejoice! Your favorite deep violet is getting a second life with Don’t Over Ink It. The shimmery, deep, inky navy-purple has all the moody, mysterious appeal of the original, but this upcoming version is shimmery rather than sparkly and leans a little more navy. Overall, though, the two are pretty dang similar. Is this your sign to revisit your purple polish era? I think yes.

According to recent reports, say bonjour to your next favorite neutral. This chic, creamy mauve-ish nude pays homage to the beloved Tickle My France-y shade. It’s more of a neutral than its predecessor, which was a much rosier, dusty-rose-meets-mauve shade. It’s soft, sophisticated, and gives your nails that effortlessly polished, je ne sais quoi look. Oui oui!

Did ya miss her? Talk about a throwback... It’s All Greek to Me is back from the archives, bringing its vivid, shimmery fuchsia pink finish along for the ride. The bold, metallic shade makes a statement, so I can see why OPI fans begged for its return. I’m ready to paint a couple coats on my fingertips ahead of the holiday party season. Who notes bright pink nails are just for summer?

I do! I do say yes to Suzi Takes a Vow. It’s a soft, romantic peachy pink that’s giving major bridal mani energy. Wedding bells or not, consider this your sign to commit to this classic light neutral.

You know when you just have to try something based on the name alone? That’s how I feel about this one. With a name like Vampire State Building, you already know this is going to be dramatic. The deep burgundy shade—originally released in 2000—delivers all the vampy energy you could want from a dark red manicure.

It has been revealed that A lot of the polishes in this fresh collection are pretty opaque, but this sheer beauty is perfect for a naked nail or soap manicure moment. It’s a soft, pale pink with a barely-there finish that’s tailor-made for the clean girl mani crowd. Think your-nails-but-better, with a little extra wink. See what I did there?

A classic red manicure never goes out of style, and neither does Vodka & Caviar (the nail polish or the food-and-drink combo). The expensive-looking shade is luxury in a bottle. This vibrant apple red looks just as good with jeans and a white tee as it does with your favorite holiday party outfit. Love some versatility!
